hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build a pipelined multiply completion lane whose register holds the full 64-bit architectural product, not the already selected 32-bit low/high result. Capture the product and high-half selection metadata on the same edge that an accepted EX multiply places its original instruction in EX/MEM. MEM owns the matching response, selects low or high product bits there, and uses that single selected architectural value for both completing-MEM forwarding and MEM/WB capture. Remove multiply from blocking EX occupancy and from the current EX bypass. This is one structural change to M-extension issue/completion ownership; preserve the ordinary RV32I pipeline, predictor, fetch topology and blocking divider.

Unlike r5s1, move low/high product selection after the product register. Preserve the shared signed 33-by-33 multiplication and explicit 66-bit intermediate: sign-extend a only for MULH/MULHSU, sign-extend b only for MULH, and retain product[63:0]. MUL reads [31:0]; MULH/MULHU/MULHSU read [63:32]. Register the selection with the accepted transaction. Do not infer separate signed/unsigned multipliers or route a combinational product into younger operand capture. Upper intermediate bits 65:64 are redundant sign extension.

Register explicit is_multiply and is_divide bits in ID/EX from the validated decoder outputs. Use these bits consistently for EX occupancy, request launch, response routing, producer eligibility and dependency interlocks instead of comparing alu_op throughout the EX-to-ID control recurrence. Retain alu_op only where the arithmetic unit needs the exact operation. The class bits are part of instruction ownership and must clear with the entire control bundle on every bubble/squash and hold with operands during stalls. Derive them only from legal decoder results; preserve default-illegal decoding and every reserved-encoding trap. This predecoded scheduling is required in the final proposal; the partial full-product prototype did not include the divide bit.

Launch a multiply only on a valid, legal EX-to-EX/MEM advance with no older dmem hold. Allow a new request on the same edge the preceding MEM-owned response is consumed, giving independent consecutive multiplies one result per cycle. Request-ready can be !response_valid || response_ready; response_ready is derived only from acceptance of the matching EX/MEM multiply, avoiding a combinational issue loop. Preserve response/product/selection until acceptance, clear validity after consumption without replacement, and invalidate all ownership on reset. Remove the redundant saved multiply EX payload and response-to-EX return path. The divider keeps its current saved payload, bounded execution, held response and blocking control.

Extend the existing load-use rule to valid EX multiplies. An immediately dependent consumer waits one bubble and then captures the actual MEM result; an independent successor advances without a multiply stall. Conservatively match both raw younger source fields to preserve exact RVFI operand values, including otherwise unused encoded fields. Include branch/JALR, effective-address, store-data and multiply/divide consumers, preserve x0 exclusion, and keep EX-over-MEM-over-write-first-RF priority. A dmem stall freezes EX/MEM and its product together and prohibits launch/replacement/consumption. A younger divider may occupy EX while an older multiply completes. Correctly predicted and mispredicted branches retain their current EX resolution and recovery latency. Squashed younger multiplies never launch; older multiplies are not canceled by younger recovery.

Capture original instruction, PC/next-PC, destination and architectural operands in the existing pipeline registers. Preserve final trap-qualified writes, accepted load extraction, cleared side-effect controls in invalid bundles, the champion's complete reset and payload/control split, bus handshakes and single channel-0 ordered retirement. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, register the exact existing operation-specific stand-in instead of a real product, using the same pipelined request/response ownership and MEM selection latency. Apply formulas to all operands. Keep the ordinary ALU's M-extension inactive real outputs and its exact ALTOPS formulas unchanged.

The expectation is fewer unnecessary multiply issue bubbles and a shorter multiply/control recurrence. The earlier pipelined-MEM experiment measured 4,238,604 CoreMark cycles, but that count is a reference, not a measurement of this final implementation. At that count, acceptance requires median Fmax above approximately 96.812 MHz and fitness above 228.405 iter/sec. The partial prototype's 93.422 MHz does not meet this bar. Predict eight percent fitness improvement with low confidence from completing operation-class retiming and moving product selection behind the register. Risks are a persistent branch/BHT limit, extra 32 product registers, physical placement and product/metadata alignment under stalls. Measure the final median and marker-bounded cycles rather than extrapolating a win. Run unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation gates, all real arithmetic suites, and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/marker/OOB validation. Preserve nret=1, exact top-level ports and every hard invariant; modify no evaluator, wrapper, benchmark or other core.

title: Remove misprediction correction from payload stall clock enables
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Localized squash clears only control,
valid and predicted_taken, but hazard_unit still makes stall_id depend
on redirect through load_use_hazard && !redirect. A vendor report from
an isolated predictor probe explicitly ends a 38-cell branch-operand
to correction path at a payload clock enable with fanout 250. Prior
folded indexing saved only 0.29 percent of cycles, and one-bit agree
prediction reduced area but lost Fmax. The remaining recovery angle is
removing redundant correction dependence from ordinary interlocks,
preserving the champion's exact predictions and two-bit hysteresis.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make fetch and ID stall requests independent of EX prediction correction.
In hazard_unit use exactly:
  stall_if = dmem_stall || ex_busy || load_use_hazard || imem_stall;
  stall_id = dmem_stall || ex_busy || load_use_hazard;
Remove the !redirect guards from these two equations. Keep flush_if,
flush_id, stall_ex_mem and hold_mem_wb unchanged. Document correction
priority at the destination registers instead of forcing stalls low.

The IF PC register already tests redirect before !stall: reset wins,
then redirect_target wins, then an unstalled prediction. An asserted
fetch stall cannot block an accepted correction, including imem
backpressure. The ID register already gives flush priority over stall
for the complete ctrl_t, valid and predicted_taken fields. A correction
may clear those fields while the payload holds; that payload is dead
until a later valid fetch replaces it. Preserve both existing priority
structures and full bubble-control clearing exactly.

An EX load-use interlock and an EX branch/jump correction are mutually
exclusive for actual decoded instructions: a correcting instruction
cannot also be the load producing the interlock. Even if both assert
in a directed control test, control flush and PC redirect still win.
Older dmem holds and arithmetic occupancy continue to defer correction
through unchanged ex_advance gating. On release, the resolving
instruction advances once and flush overrides ID control hold. This
removes correction from the high-fanout ID payload clock enable and
ordinary fetch-stall generation without adding a bubble or stage.

Retain the 128x2 predictor, PC[8:2] indexing, instruction qualification,
aligned direct targets, saved predicted_taken, direction-XOR recovery,
aligned JAL prediction, sequential JALR and once-per-advance training.
Preserve complete reset, held registered operands, forwarding,
RV32M/ALTOPS logic, decoder and alignment traps, memory handshakes,
nret=1 IO, strict RVFI order and resolved architectural next PC. Do not
introduce another predictor/table, training pipeline or arithmetic change.

Expect eight percent higher fitness from Fmax at unchanged CoreMark
cycles. Acceptance requires more than 228.40456 iter/sec, equivalent
to more than 98.133 MHz at unchanged cycles. Competing ALU/forwarding
paths may limit the gain, so confidence is low pending vendor timing.
Validate correction during unavailable imem, after older dmem holds,
around load-use bubbles and blocking arithmetic, and on trained loop
exits. Require exact RVFI PCs/next PCs/results/order/traps, complete
control clearing, operand retention and no wrong-path memory effects.
Run unchanged formal/cosim and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO
checks, then score median Gowin Fmax times marker-bounded iter/cycle.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

Changed the hazard-unit equations exactly as proposed:

- `stall_if = dmem_stall || ex_busy || load_use_hazard || imem_stall`
- `stall_id = dmem_stall || ex_busy || load_use_hazard`

The flush equations and downstream holds are unchanged. Added comments at the
hazard unit and destination registers documenting reset/redirect/stall PC
priority and complete control/valid/prediction flush priority over ID stall.
IF and ID register logic, predictor, execution, memory, and RVFI are unchanged.

Retained all existing tests. Strengthened pipeline checks to verify PC priority
on every edge and asserted fetch stall during unavailable-imem corrections,
including after older memory holds and load-use bubbles. Added a trained loop
exit with older memory stalls, load-use bubbles, blocking division, exact RVFI
PCs/results/order/traps, once-per-advance training, and accepted memory effects.
Added an exhaustive hazard-unit test covering 1,152 input combinations, including
synthetic simultaneous redirect/load-use and older holds. Existing ID-stage
tests check every stall/flush/valid combination, full control clearing, and
payload retention. No architectural deviations from the hypothesis.

Local validation:

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings.
- `make bench` then `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS, all five ELFs;
  unstalled/stalled selftest and three random-program RVFI comparisons, plus
  canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/out-of-bounds validation.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  PASS, 53 checks passed, 0 failed, first attempt; auto-selected nret=1 wrapper
  and ALTOPS configuration. No counterexamples or RTL fix attempts.
- Full cocotb suite: PASS, all 14 pytest runners / 117 cocotb cases, including
  real RV32M and ALTOPS tests and the new trained-exit and exhaustive hazard cases.
- Gowin timing: all three canonical placement options successfully routed.
  Fmax: option 0 = 83.220 MHz, option 1 = 87.205 MHz, option 2 = 87.205 MHz;
  median = 87.205 MHz. Logic = 3,720; registers = 1,090.
- Canonical CoreMark: 10 iterations, exactly 4,296,444 marker-bounded cycles,
  2.3275061888389562e-6 iterations/cycle, matching the champion's cycle count.
- Fitness = 202.97 iterations/second, below the required 228.40456. The
  hypothesis did not achieve the timing/fitness acceptance threshold.

The median-option worst path remains 38 cells from registered EX rs2 through
EX logic named `redirect_Z`, ID operand selection (`rs2_value`), and the ID
ALU-input register's D pin. The stall equations no longer depend on correction,
but a competing operand-selection path remains. No arithmetic or forwarding
changes were made to chase timing beyond the requested hypothesis.
lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r7s2 (regression, -7.05%): With PC redirect and ID control flush already overriding stalls, removing redirect from stall_if/stall_id preserves CoreMark cycles but leaves the 38-cell EX rs2-to-ID ALU-input D path through redirect_Z and rs2_value, so clock-enable simplification alone can regress Fmax.

title: Match forwarding destinations in parallel using one held M tag
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Its ordinary ALU result and blocking
multiply/divide responses share one EX bypass data bus, destination
bus and write enable. The current destination is selected from in.rd,
multiply_payload_q.rd and divide_payload_q.rd before forward_unit
compares it with each ID source. Vendor probes repeatedly expose an
operation-decode to destination-selection to equality to ID-operand
path. The round-7 operation-tag recoding lost 8.68 percent, while the
round-6 six-candidate data crossbar increased LUTs and lost 6.40 percent.
A local Boolean refactoring of destination matching can remove that
serial control prefix without widening the data crossbar.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Its ordinary ALU result and blocking
multiply/divide responses share one EX bypass data bus, destination
bus and write enable. The current destination is selected from in.rd,
multiply_payload_q.rd and divide_payload_q.rd before forward_unit
compares it with each ID source. Vendor probes repeatedly expose an
operation-decode to destination-selection to equality to ID-operand
path. The round-7 operation-tag recoding lost 8.68 percent, while the
round-6 six-candidate data crossbar increased LUTs and lost 6.40 percent.
A local Boolean refactoring of destination matching can remove that

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compute each EX producer's destination match independently, then combine
the accepted matches. Preserve the existing shared bypass data bus and
existing two-bit RF/EX/MEM selection consumed by ID. This changes only
forwarding-control implementation, not stage boundaries, arithmetic
protocols, pipeline scheduling, register-file behavior or prediction.

Add the two raw ID source addresses as inputs to ex_stage. Capture one
five-bit arithmetic_rd_q on mul_launch or div_launch; reset it to zero
and otherwise retain it until the next launch. EX permits only one
outstanding M instruction, so this tag is the captured destination for
either accepted response. Keep both existing full arithmetic metadata
records. Use the common tag for an arithmetic bypass destination and
override EX/MEM.rd with this tag on either arithmetic transfer, allowing
the duplicated timed destination fields to be pruned. Do not merge the
full records or change their capture, validity or response-hold behavior.

For each source s, compare s in parallel with in.rd and arithmetic_rd_q.
Form three scalar producer enables directly from
the existing conditions, without using the selected bypass_rd bus:
  ordinary = ex_advance && !is_multiply && !is_divide
             && ctrl_with_trap.reg_write
             && !ctrl_with_trap.is_illegal && !ctrl_with_trap.mem_read;
  multiply = ex_advance && is_multiply && mul_transfer
             && multiply_payload_q.valid
             && multiply_payload_q.ctrl.reg_write
             && !multiply_payload_q.ctrl.is_illegal
             && !multiply_payload_q.ctrl.mem_read;
  divide = ex_advance && is_divide && div_transfer
           && divide_payload_q.valid
           && divide_payload_q.ctrl.reg_write
           && !divide_payload_q.ctrl.is_illegal
           && !divide_payload_q.ctrl.mem_read.
Then export:
  match_s = (s != 0) &&
            ((ordinary && in.rd == s)
             || ((multiply || divide) && arithmetic_rd_q == s)).
A matched destination is automatically nonzero because s is nonzero;
do not introduce another selected-destination zero check into this path.
Preserve the explicit class exclusion on ordinary and exact existing
M-class decoding. Do not replace final trap-adjusted write qualification
with an assumption about legal instruction controls.

Wire the qualified EX matches into forward_unit. For each source choose
EX when its EX match is true, otherwise the unchanged completing MEM
match, otherwise RF. Retain EX-over-MEM-over-RF priority and the existing
fwd_rs1/fwd_rs2 encodings. Keep ID's operand muxes, x0 enforcement and
final alu_a/alu_b capture exactly unchanged. Keep bypass_data selection
and the saved arithmetic records unchanged: both M responses still
forward their captured launch destination, including during response
holds. Existing bypass_rd/bypass_w_en outputs may remain for stage tests
and equivalence checks; core forwarding must no longer consume them,
so unused legacy destination-selection logic is pruned in the timed
netlist. Preserve all top-level core ports and nret=1.

The equivalence target is match_s == old_bypass_w_en &&
old_bypass_rd == s && s != 0 for every source and control combination
permitted by the existing disjoint operation classes. Also prove that
the held tag equals the active saved destination from launch through
transfer, including stalls and reset cancellation. Check the match
identity with symbolic operands, destinations and producer controls
under this proved state invariant. Two small
destination candidates now run alongside operation/acceptance decoding,
rather than after a five-bit destination mux. This should shorten
control arrival at the existing ID operand selection without adding
the six full-width masked data candidates that regressed in round 6.

Expect eight percent higher fitness from Fmax, with low confidence
because branch recovery and accepted-load forwarding remain competing
paths. An initial prototype comparing all three destinations separately
reached only 90.203 MHz and increased LUTs to 3,881. It is not an accepted
result. The proposed refinement instead uses the single held M tag to
remove duplicate M comparisons and timed saved-destination selection;
this refinement remains unmeasured and requires full evaluation.
Require unchanged 4,296,444 canonical measured cycles; acceptance
needs more than 228.40456 iter/sec, or approximately 98.133 MHz median
Fmax at that cycle count. Measure all three canonical Gowin placement
options and inspect the destination-match path. Local comparator,
shifter, metadata-sharing and wider one-hot selection probes did not
establish a gain on this champion; do not include those changes.

Keep exact real RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic, launch-once ownership,
held responses, registered architectural operands, memory handshakes,
decoder default-illegal validation, branch/memory alignment traps,
predictor training, reset/flush/hold priorities, RVFI fields and strict
retirement order. Retain every existing test assertion. Run unchanged
formal, stalled RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC, validation

title: Resolve control-flow recovery from registered EX/MEM transactions
motivation:
The champion reaches 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Recent forwarding-crossbar, multiply
completion and recovery clock-enable attempts lost 5-7 percent. Their
worst paths repeatedly run from registered EX rs2 through branch/recovery
logic into ID operands or the fetch predictor, with about 38 cells.
Merely simplifying the consumers has not removed this operand-to-global-
control timing cone. The successful operand and multiply retiming rounds
show that establishing a real register boundary can outperform local mux
changes. The older elastic-fetch experiment paid an extra refill cycle;
this proposal instead registers recovery itself while retaining the current
combinational fetch/decode interface and correctly predicted throughput.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move control-flow correction and branch-predictor training from advancing
EX to acceptance of the existing EX/MEM transaction in MEM. EX still
computes conditional-branch direction, JAL/JALR destinations, alignment
faults and architectural next-PC, but registers the correction-needed bit,
correction target, branch update enable/index and actual outcome alongside
that instruction in EX/MEM. Fetch, decode squash and BHT writes consume
only these registered records. This is one structural change to the
control-transfer resolution boundary, not a new predictor or another
multiply pipeline. Retain the present two-bit direction predictor, its
indexing and reset state, direct-JAL prediction, fetch topology, ordinary
ALU latency, existing operand forwarding, and blocking RV32M units.

A valid accepted EX/MEM control transfer emits its recovery and training
event exactly once. Use MEM acceptance, not merely occupancy; an older
dmem hold cannot replay an event or let it overtake an older transaction.
Compute the saved mismatch with the current direction-XOR policy: actual
nonsequential execution is legal, aligned taken branch or legal aligned
jump; a mismatch also restores sequential execution after a misaligned
predicted target. Carry the correct architectural pc_next and final trap
controls for RVFI independently of whether a redirect is necessary.
Predictor training uses the current counter at the saved branch index,
preserving saturation and updating only a legal aligned conditional branch.

On registered MEM correction, redirect PC and squash both younger slots:
the current ID/EX instruction and the raw fetched instruction. Suppress
that younger EX instruction's EX/MEM advance, bypass write enable,
multiplier/divider request, saved arithmetic payload capture, and any
branch record. Insert an invalid EX/MEM bubble with every side-effect
control cleared. Clear ID/EX controls, valid and prediction state; preserve
the champion's payload-hold/reset policy. Correction overrides load-use,
imem unavailability and younger EX occupancy. The correcting instruction
itself still advances to MEM/WB and retires once. A correctly predicted
control transfer causes no squash or extra bubble. A misprediction or
unpredicted JALR costs one additional recovery cycle relative to the
champion; measure its frequency rather than assuming unchanged IPC.

Keep branch comparisons out of ordinary advancing-EX producer eligibility.
Conditional branches never write a register: qualify ALU writes from legal
registered controls, valid, acceptance and operation class, and qualify
link writes separately with the low-bit jump-alignment check. Do not feed
the general branch_cond/branch_taken cone through ctrl_with_trap into the
EX bypass enable or M-unit launch eligibility. Architectural final trap
metadata still includes every branch/jump alignment fault. This is required
to make the new recovery boundary a real timing cut rather than leave an
equivalent operand-to-ID path through write qualification. Preserve
EX-over-MEM-over-write-first-RF forwarding and exact captured RVFI operands.

Retain launch-once and held-result behavior for multiplication/division,
including the existing exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS stand-ins. A younger M
instruction cannot launch on a MEM-correction cycle. Once an M request has
actually launched, no older unresolved control-transfer record may remain;
enforce that ownership relationship and reset all pending state. Do not
cancel an older arithmetic result due to a younger event. Preserve stalled
load extraction, memory masks, trap-qualified writes, retirement order,
default-illegal decoding, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, nret=1 and all IO.

Predict a 12 percent fitness improvement with medium confidence: removing
the repeated branch-to-recovery-to-operand path should allow an appreciable
Fmax gain while only incorrect predictions pay the extra cycle. This is
unmeasured. For example, at a three percent cycle increase, acceptance
needs more than approximately 101.1 MHz; 110 MHz at that cycle count would
yield roughly 248.6 iterations/sec. The ordinary ALU-to-ID feedback may
become the new limit, and delayed predictor updates or physical placement
may consume the gain. Evaluate final median Gowin Fmax and actual bracketed
cycles against the 228.405 iterations/sec acceptance threshold. Run the
unchanged formal and RVFI cosimulation gates, real arithmetic suites, and
stalled canonical CoreMark CRC, UART, marker and OOB validation. No wrapper,
benchmark, evaluator, contract file or other core is changed.

title: Register lookahead direction lookup without adding a fetch stage
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Folded indexing saved only 0.29 percent
of cycles, and one-bit agree prediction, smaller tables and recovery
enable simplifications have not beaten the champion. Fetch currently
reads a 128-way counter mux combinationally before choosing its next
address. Registering the direction for the PC being entered can remove
that table read from the current prediction/PC-selection path while
preserving instruction throughput and the existing pipeline depth.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the 128-entry two-bit saturating BHT, but move its fetch read into
a registered lookahead path. Add a two-bit direction_q in if_stage.
Current legal conditional-branch prediction uses direction_q[1], while
aligned JAL prediction and instruction-derived targets remain unchanged.
Do not add an instruction register, a pipeline stage, cached targets,
global history, a return stack or a new recovery protocol.

Derive lookahead_index = next_pc[8:2], where next_pc is the existing
completed-address selection using the current registered direction.
On a non-reset, non-redirect edge with !stall, load direction_q from
counters[lookahead_index]. When stall holds the PC, hold direction_q too.
Do not select held PC versus next PC before the table read: that adds
the EX-recovery-dependent stall signal to the lookup-address path.
The same advancing edge changes PC and its saved direction together.
Only the low seven address bits feed this lookup: upper target-adder
carry propagation must not enter the counter-read endpoint. This creates
PC/instruction-to-lookahead-index-to-two-bit-register timing instead of
table-read-to-current-prediction-to-PC timing. Keep target and PC+4
additions parallel and select their completed addresses.

Reset direction_q to 2'b01. On an accepted EX redirect also set it to
2'b01 while the PC takes redirect_target with its existing priority.
This explicit weakly-not-taken fallback avoids connecting the long
EX correction/target path through another BHT lookup in the same cycle.
It affects only conditional guesses at the first recovered instruction;
aligned JAL is still predicted directly. The next ordinary edge reads
ahead from the fallback's selected address. Never use a counter belonging
to the abandoned pre-correction address after recovery.

During imem, load-use, dmem and arithmetic stalls, PC and direction_q
both hold; table training may continue for an independently advancing
older branch. This preserves one stable guess until fetch acceptance.
An unavailable or squashed fetch still has invalid control. If EX trains
the same entry on the advancing sampling edge, direction_q receives the
old counter under nonblocking assignment semantics; no outcome bypass
is added. This bounded staleness can change accuracy, but EX verifies
the exact predicted_taken bit captured with each accepted instruction.
Keep saturation based on the live training counter, not direction_q,
and train exactly once on the unchanged legal aligned EX acceptance.

Preserve instruction qualification and direct-target alignment gating,
accepted predicted_taken/direct_target metadata, direction-XOR recovery,
architectural next-PC reporting, complete control/valid/prediction
squash, payload retention, correction priority and memory handshakes.
Keep every EX, arithmetic, forwarding, hazard and decoder implementation
unchanged, including real RV32M/ALTOPS, all traps, nret=1 IO, consecutive
RVFI order and wrong-path side-effect suppression.

path and existing operand feedback may limit vendor Fmax. At unchanged

cycles require median Fmax_Hz * 10 / measured_cycles above 228.40456.

all younger controls, and no wrong-path stores occur. Run unchanged

Gowin timing. Prototype evidence does not replace implementation gates.

title: Update saturating branch counters locally without a training read mux
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
measured CoreMark cycles. Recent forwarding, clock-enable and predictor
changes have not exceeded its fitness. A fresh vendor synthesis report
attributes 849 LUTs and 288 registers to fetch, including its resettable
128-entry two-bit BHT. The current variable-index training expression
reads a counter, tests saturation, increments or decrements it, and routes
the result back to one entry. Branch-to-counter-update paths repeatedly
appear among the limiting timing paths. Preserve the prediction algorithm
and optimize only this expensive state-update implementation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the BHT's variable-index read/modify/write training block with
128 statically generated local two-bit saturating counter updates. Keep
the same table, PC[8:2] index, weakly-not-taken reset state, combinational
fetch lookup, branch acceptance event and instruction-qualified prediction.
No prediction, instruction latency or pipeline boundary changes.

For entry i, its write enable is branch_update && branch_index == i.
On reset write 2'b01. Otherwise, on that enable, update from that entry's
own registered bits q1:q0 using these exact equations:
  next_q1 = branch_taken ? (q1 | q0) : (q1 & q0);
  next_q0 = branch_taken ? (q1 | ~q0) : (q1 & ~q0).
Use one-bit expressions for bitwise complement. Taken implements
00->01->10->11->11; not-taken implements 11->10->01->00->00.
Every other entry holds. Use static generate indices and separate
clocked ownership for each entry, allowing Gowin to map the local
two-input update functions and index-qualified enables directly.
Do not select counters[branch_index] into a shared training datapath,
infer a variable-index write data broadcast, or add saturation arithmetic.

This is a Boolean micro-optimization of the existing state machine,
not a predictor-policy change. Unlike the earlier one-bit agree proposal,
it preserves all four counter states, hysteresis, reset values and exact
same-edge read/write behavior. Fetch prediction sees the old counter
before the active edge and the updated value afterward, just as before.
Training still occurs exactly once on accepted legal aligned EX branches,
including both taken and not-taken outcomes; stalls and correction have
their existing precedence. Keep direct JAL/JALR treatment, target alignment,
saved prediction metadata and direction-XOR recovery unchanged.

Preserve every other RTL module, real RV32M and exact ALTOPS behavior,
nret=1 ports, decoder default-illegal validation, architectural operand
capture, trap-qualified side effects, memory handshakes, consecutive RVFI
order and all hard invariants. Prove each local transition matches the
original saturating update for all four states and both outcomes, then
check table hold, reset, aliasing and accepted-event behavior in fetch and
pipeline tests. Retain every existing test assertion.

Expect eight percent greater fitness through lower logic and routing cost,
with low confidence because ALU and load forwarding remain competing
limits. Require unchanged 4,296,444 canonical marker-bounded cycles and
exact prediction traces for identical branch events. Acceptance requires
more than 228.40456 iterations/sec, approximately 98.133 MHz median Fmax
at that cycle count. Run all three canonical Gowin placement options and
the unchanged formal, stalled RVFI cosimulation, real arithmetic and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO/bracket/bounded-memory gates. Prototype
timing is preliminary and does not replace those implementation gates.

title: Decouple predicted fetch with an independently written circular instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz with 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Its IF/ID interface is combinational:
each instruction-bus stall immediately bubbles decode, while load-use,
blocking arithmetic and data-bus holds stop fetching altogether. With
independent approximately 22 percent bus stalls, these missed fetch
opportunities matter. The earlier structural fetch-register attempt
r2s1 improved Fmax 14.39 percent but increased cycles 6.45 percent; it
preceded the successful direct-branch/JAL predictor, so taken branches
repeatedly paid its refill penalty. Recent result-mux and recovery
rewrites have failed to clear the acceptance bar. A predicted, buffered
frontend now offers a different tradeoff: fetch ahead during backend
holds, preserve predicted targets, and register the instruction before
decoder/register-file reads. The r8s1 deferred-recovery result also
shows that an extra correction cycle alone can consume a modest Fmax
gain, so both actual cycles and timing must improve the final product.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the live combinational IF/ID interface with a strict, two-entry
circular FIFO of accepted predicted fetch transactions. Each entry owns its PC,
instruction, predicted_taken and direct_target. Keep the existing
instruction-qualified 128-entry two-bit BHT, direct-JAL prediction,
indexing, initialization and once-per-accepted-EX training. Prediction
and next-PC calculation occur when a fetch is enqueued, never when its
instruction is dequeued. This is one structural change to frontend
buffering and pipeline elasticity; it adds no cache or new predictor.

Use two stationary payload slots and one-bit registered head/tail
pointers. Write only the tail slot on a fetch-space/ready opportunity;
dequeue advances the head pointer rather than copying a wide tail
payload into a head register. A registered-head-selected mux exposes
the stored instruction. Separate payload writes from occupancy and
correction control. Payload opportunity enables depend on imemReady,
registered capacity and raw issue-hold reasons, never on redirect or
branch operand comparison. Reset payloads fully, but let an inactive
slot capture harmless data on a correction edge; occupancy/pointers
flush and PC redirect, so that data is never admitted or retired.
Correction only controls ownership, not wide payload clock enables.
Derive raw issue hold from load-use, EX busy and dmem hold without a
redirect term; control squash still overrides every architectural pop.

Separate fetch acceptance from instruction issue. Enqueue only when
io_imemReady is high, reset/correction is absent, and a queue slot is
available. Advance the fetch PC exactly once per accepted enqueue.
With a full FIFO and no dequeue, keep the address and queue stable.
Allow simultaneous enqueue/dequeue, including replacing an entry in a
full queue, without a combinational data fall-through. Decode sees
only registered head payload and occupancy. An empty FIFO may enqueue
this edge but cannot issue that new instruction until the next cycle;
do not bypass io_imemData into decode to regain this cycle.

Load-use interlocks, EX multiply/divide occupancy and older dmem
backpressure hold issue, but do not stop fetch while the FIFO has room.
Conversely, io_imemReady=0 prevents enqueue/PC advance but must not
flush or hold an already buffered head instruction. Pop exactly when
ID/EX actually accepts a valid head. During a load-use bubble retain
that head for the subsequent completing-MEM load bypass. During a
blocking M operation retain head and resolved ID/EX operands, allow
older MEM/WB work to drain, and fetch up to queue capacity. Once a
hold ends, the next buffered instruction can issue even if the current
instruction bus is stalled. Preserve the existing single-cycle ordinary
ALU, one-bubble load-use and blocking RV32M request/response behavior.

An accepted EX correction has priority over both enqueue and dequeue:
invalidate both queued entries, kill the younger ID/EX admission, set
fetch PC to redirect_target, and discard any old-address response on
that edge. Do not retain wrong-path instructions or permit a queued
store/M operation to issue during correction. An older dmem hold still
defers EX advance and therefore defers correction as today. Correctly
predicted branches/JAL never flush the queue; their target instruction
is fetched ahead and follows in order. Store prediction metadata with
its own instruction, rather than reconstructing it from the newer
fetch PC. The actual retiring pc_next remains resolved in EX. Expect
one extra refill cycle for a prediction correction or unpredicted
JALR, but no compulsory extra cycle for a correct prediction.

title: Four-bank bimodal predictor with registered training transactions
motivation: The 218.36 iter/sec champion already predicts direct branches and JAL. Reference profiling finds only 13,735 returns in the timed region, limiting perfect return prediction to about 0.32 percent cycle savings. Prior folded indexing saved only 0.29 percent of cycles; agree and registered-lookup designs reduced Fmax. Recent timing paths repeatedly run from EX branch operands through the predictor counter update, with 37-38 cells. The current counter update consumes the live combinational branch outcome. Registering the accepted training transaction can break this timing path while preserving the working predictor's size, hysteresis, index and fetch latency. Isolated prototypes found that banking alone reduced area by 152 LUTs and 128 flip-flops but reached only 89.252 MHz, and posting training into the original flop table reached only 84.355 MHz. The proposed combination targets both predictor routing/state pressure and the combinational training prefix; neither isolated optimization is claimed to beat the champion. A combined eight-bank prototype reached 90.097 MHz with 3,520 LUTs and 971 FFs; it also failed to beat the champion and shifted the worst path to MEM load forwarding. The final hypothesis uses four 32-row banks to reduce global lookup selection and bank write-control fanout. This final bank geometry has not been timed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one pipeline register for conditional-branch training inside if_stage, between the existing EX acceptance interface and a compact banked BHT update port. Save train_valid_q, the seven-bit branch_index, and branch_taken. On every non-reset edge set train_valid_q to the current branch_update; capture index/outcome when branch_update is true. Reset train_valid_q to zero and retain the BHT's logical reset to weakly not taken. Index/outcome payload need not reset because an invalid transaction never writes the table.

At the same edge, apply the previously registered transaction to the 128-entry two-bit table. Compute saturation from the LIVE counter at train_index_q on the application cycle, incrementing for train_taken_q and decrementing otherwise. Do not capture a precomputed next counter: consecutive branches or aliases at the same index must see the preceding applied write and preserve update order. This one-entry pipeline consumes an older transaction and captures a new one every cycle, so it needs no full/ready signal and supports one accepted branch per cycle without dropping or repeating updates.

The register captures exactly the existing valid, legal, aligned EX-to-EX/MEM branch acceptance event. Keep ex_stage's branch_update/index/outcome generation and all pipeline stages unchanged. A transaction that was already accepted must drain exactly once even if the following cycle has an imem stall, dmem hold, load-use interlock, arithmetic wait or EX correction. These younger conditions must not hold or replay train_valid_q. Bubbles capture an invalid transaction; reset discards any queued event and resets the table. The table may update during a later pipeline hold because its transaction belongs to an already accepted instruction.

Implement the BHT as four explicitly generated banks of thirty-two two-bit counter payloads. Select bank with index[6:5] and row with index[4:0], retaining PC[8:2] for both fetch and training. Each bank has a 32-bit resettable valid vector; its counter payload array has no reset so Gowin can infer asynchronous-read, synchronous-write LUT RAM. An invalid fetch or update row behaves as 2'b01. The first queued taken update therefore writes 2'b10, and a not-taken update writes 2'b00. Read fetch and training rows independently. Select completed bank counters for fetch, parallel with the existing target additions. Payload writes are unconditional on saturation whenever !reset && train_valid_q selects the bank; compute next_counter combinationally from the current valid-qualified row and write even when the saturated value is unchanged. Reset and update validity in a separate always_ff block. Preserve bank/row shape and this memory inference pattern; do not replace it with vendor primitives or reset counter arrays.


Fetch keeps the existing combinational lookup at PC[8:2], instruction qualification, aligned direct target, always-taken direct JAL, sequential JALR, and completed-address selection. No folded index, alternative counter encoding, outcome-to-fetch bypass or registered fetch lookup. The only prediction-policy change is one cycle later learning. Same-edge table reads observe the pre-write state under the existing nonblocking semantics. Fetch/ID must continue carrying the exact predicted_taken used when the instruction is accepted; ordinary EX direction-XOR recovery makes delayed guesses architecturally harmless.

This splits registered EX operands to comparator to training register from registered training to counter read/saturation/write, removing the long comparator prefix and its fanout from table-write timing. Keep correction in EX with its existing latency, preserve every payload/control hold and squash rule, top-level nret=1 ports, architectural operands and resolved RVFI PC, illegal and misalignment traps, link write suppression, real M arithmetic, memory handshakes and consecutive retirement order. No benchmark, contract, wrapper, tool or other-core change.

Expect approximately six percent higher fitness if decoupling predictor training raises Fmax beyond the 4.6 percent acceptance margin, with a small warmup/aliasing cycle cost possible from delayed learning. This is a low-confidence forecast for the unmeasured four-bank refinement; none of the measured related prototypes cleared acceptance. Confidence is low because the unchanged ALU/forwarding and branch-recovery cones may still limit timing. Require measured median Fmax_Hz times 10 divided by marker-bounded CoreMark cycles above 228.40456 iter/sec; at unchanged cycles this needs more than 98.133 MHz. Test same-index consecutive updates, alternating outcomes, saturation, aliasing, reset with a pending event, and a pending write coincident with every hold/correction cause. Verify exactly one applied write per accepted branch and the delayed predictor's exact predictions, then unchanged full formal/cosim gates and all canonical CRC/UART/MMIO checks.

Cover invalid uninitialized payload masking, every bank/row, reset and first-update behavior, simultaneous fetch/update on different rows and banks, and same-row old-data behavior.

Verify queued updates correspond exactly once and in order to accepted legal aligned branches, including independent bus stalls, load-use holds, M occupancy and recovery. Preserve exact RVFI PC/result/trap/order and wrong-path-store assertions and check predictions against the delayed-training model.

title: Fuse immediate selection into the ID ALU-B forwarding mux
motivation:
The champion's limiting path runs from registered EX ALU operands through
the ALU and forwarding back to the ID/EX ALU inputs. ID currently resolves
a three-source rs2_value, forces x0, then selects immediate versus that
result for alu_b. This serial selection adds another mux to a timed
recurrence. Previous opcode recoding, predictor updates and the six-source
direct EX result crossbar all regressed; the latter increased LUTs to
3,887. A smaller change confined to final ALU-B selection can remove one
serial mux while retaining the shared EX bypass and producer qualification.
A local experiment fusing both ALU-A and ALU-B selection passed the
existing ID/pipeline suites but reached only 92.375 MHz median, below the
93.817 MHz champion. The proposed narrower ALU-B-only circuit avoids the
additional AUIPC/ALU-A crossbar and its routing pressure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the combinational source selection feeding reg_q.alu_b with
a four-candidate mutually exclusive masked-OR mux. Derive its scalar
selects in parallel from dec_alu_src, fwd_rs2_sel and the raw rs2 address:
  immediate = dec_alu_src;
  ex = !dec_alu_src && rs2_addr != 0 && fwd_rs2_sel == 1;
  mem = !dec_alu_src && rs2_addr != 0 && fwd_rs2_sel == 2;
  rf = !dec_alu_src && rs2_addr != 0
       && fwd_rs2_sel != 1 && fwd_rs2_sel != 2.
Compute alu_b_value as the bitwise OR of imm masked by immediate,
fwd_ex_data masked by ex, fwd_mem_data masked by mem, and rs2_data masked
by rf. Capture this value into the existing ID/EX alu_b register on its
unchanged payload clock enable. Express the four masks directly so the
source-mode gate can merge into source selection; do not select rs2_value
and then put a second full-width immediate mux after it.

Leave rs2_value and its architectural rs2_val capture exactly unchanged
for stores, branches, divider operands and RVFI. Leave ALU-A, AUIPC,
rs1_value, EX bypass data/destination/enable, M ownership and both saved
arithmetic payloads unchanged. The candidates are the existing shared EX
result, completing MEM result, write-first RF and immediate; do not expose
separate ALU/MUL/DIV candidates or repeat the six-source crossbar.
Existing forwarding control still enforces EX-over-MEM-over-RF priority
and acceptance/trap qualification. For reserved selector 3, preserve
default-to-RF behavior. For register-source x0 all data masks are zero;
for an immediate-source instruction imm is selected even when rs2_addr
is zero. Preserve shifts and sign-extended immediates without changing
ALU arithmetic or operation tags.

This is a single combinational operand-mux micro-optimization, with no
added registers, pipeline boundaries or instruction latency. Preserve
complete reset, payload hold, control squash and fetch-invalid priorities.
Selected alu_b must equal the original expression for every combination
of all source values, selector, source mode and x0. Keep nret=1 IO,
decoder default-illegal validation, alignment traps, exact real RV32M
and ALTOPS results, memory handshakes, architectural operands and
strictly consecutive RVFI retirement order.

Expect six percent higher fitness from a shorter final ALU-B selection,
with low confidence because ALU-A, branch recovery and accepted-load
forwarding can remain limiting. The broader measured prototype was not
an accepted improvement; it does not establish a gain for this narrower
circuit. Require unchanged 4,296,444 canonical measured CoreMark cycles
and median vendor Fmax above approximately 98.133 MHz, giving fitness
above 228.40456 iter/sec to clear the 4.6 percent margin. Measure all
three canonical Gowin placement options. Run unchanged formal, stalled
RVFI cosimulation and CoreMark gates, including all canonical CRCs, the
validation literal, bounded memory and MMIO timing brackets. Modify no
evaluator, wrapper, benchmark, contract or other core.

title: Retiming carry preparation and execution classes across ID/EX
motivation:
The champion achieves 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz with
4,296,444 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent structural attempts leave
EX arithmetic and result forwarding into ID/EX as a recurring timing
limit. r8s1 moved recovery into MEM but added 67,904 cycles and scored
217.64; r9s1 buffered fetch and scored 225.27, below the 4.6 percent
acceptance threshold. Isolated fall-through queue experiments in this
proposal turn reduced cycles but lost enough vendor Fmax to regress.
The next promising structural target is the arithmetic register boundary,
with unchanged instruction latency, rather than another frontend buffer.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion achieves 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz with
4,296,444 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent structural attempts leave
EX arithmetic and result forwarding into ID/EX as a recurring timing
limit. r8s1 moved recovery into MEM but added 67,904 cycles and scored
217.64; r9s1 buffered fetch and scored 225.27, below the 4.6 percent
acceptance threshold. Isolated fall-through queue experiments in this
proposal turn reduced cycles but lost enough vendor Fmax to regress.
The next promising structural target is the arithmetic register boundary,
with unchanged instruction latency, rather than another frontend buffer.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming one shared add/subtract/compare datapath across the existing
ID/EX register is the entire architectural hypothesis. Keep fetch,
prediction, stage count, blocking multiplier/divider and dependency
interlocks as in the champion. ID still resolves architectural operands
with EX-over-MEM-over-write-first-RF priority and selects final ALU inputs.
Alongside the existing registered operands, capture bitwise carry
preparation rather than doing a multi-bit addition before the register.

For legal ADD, ADDI, address generation, AUIPC and JALR use a=alu_a,
b=alu_b and s=0. SUB, SLT/SLTI, SLTU/SLTIU and conditional branches use
s=1. A conditional branch's selected inputs are its architectural rs1
and rs2. Form p = a XOR b XOR {32{s}} and g = a AND (b XOR {32{s}}),
and register p, g and s together with the owning instruction. These
are bit-local operations with no carry chain in ID. Retain the original
alu_a/alu_b and architectural source values for other ALU operations,
RV32M units, store data, signs and exact RVFI operands. The preparation
registers must follow the existing payload reset, advance and stall-hold
policy, with validity and side effects governed by the original controls.

Register execution classes on the same boundary as preparation. Derive
is_multiply, is_divide, use_prepared_arithmetic, arithmetic_compare and
signed_compare from validated decoder outputs in ID. Carry these with
ctrl_t, clear them on every squash/bubble and hold them with the owning
instruction. Use registered multiply/divide classes for busy, launch,
response and bypass routing, and the prepared/compare classes for result
selection. Do not repeatedly decode five-bit alu_op in the EX-to-ID
feedback path. Retain exact alu_op for the M unit request and nonarithmetic
ALU. This is necessary control retiming for the new arithmetic boundary;
r7s1's class retiming alone regressed and is not evidence of a gain here.

EX consumes registered p/g/s to produce sum, carry-out and comparisons.
Use a sparse balanced carry structure: eight four-bit groups with local
group generate/propagate, a balanced group prefix and bounded local carry
reconstruction. Avoid a dense all-bit prefix with long global wiring and
avoid a serial 32-bit ripple recurrence. Use registered class bits for
the final arithmetic-versus-other and comparison-versus-sum muxes.
The associative combine is (Ghi OR Phi*Glo, Phi*Plo); each carry is the
prefix generate OR prefix propagate*s. Sum bits are p XOR carry-in.
Unsigned less-than for subtraction is NOT final carry-out. Signed
less-than uses operand signs when they differ, otherwise unsigned
less-than. For a subtract-prepared branch, all p bits being one means
equality; use that and the same signed/unsigned carry comparison for
all six conditional branches. Route JALR target addition through this
same prepared arithmetic result, then clear bit zero and retain the
existing bit-one alignment fault. Keep PC+4 and saved direct targets
on their existing paths.

The shared combinational alu module must retain its ordinary default
interface behavior for existing unit tests. A constant parameter or
separate nonarithmetic execution module may disable ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU
inside the core's ALU instance, whose results now come from the prepared
prefix lane. Synthesis must actually remove those duplicate full-width
arithmetic paths. Retain bitwise operations and barrel shifts at their
current latency, and preserve every real M-extension and ALTOPS formula.
Do not move M arithmetic into the new carry lane or change its handshakes.

The structural benefit is moving initial bit carry preparation before
ID/EX while avoiding a long arithmetic cone after forwarding in ID.
A tested preliminary variant registered four eight-bit carry-select
sums, but its ordinary ID addition made timing substantially worse:
61.752 MHz on placement option zero despite correct CoreMark at exactly
4,296,444 cycles. Do not implement that variant, nor compute sum1 by
incrementing a captured-candidate sum0 before ID/EX. A second prototype registered bitwise p/g and used a dense five-level
prefix, but retained repeated alu_op class decoding. It passed stalled
RVFI comparison for selftest and all three random programs (115, 11,037,
11,094 and 12,059 retirements), and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker
checks at exactly 4,296,444 cycles. Placement option zero reached only
74.857 MHz, with 3,824 logic cells and 1,123 registers. Its worst path was
18.653 ns through 13 cells from ID/EX alu_op to a preparation register,
via EX result selection and forwarding. It is a measured regression.
The final proposal explicitly differs by registering execution classes
and using the sparse group carry structure; neither its timing nor its
fitness has been measured. Do not reproduce either failed prototype or
claim their correctness checks establish the final implementation.

No instruction gains a stage or an execution bubble. Keep the original
EX forwarding acceptance, final trap qualification, branch correction
latency, once-per-accepted branch training, dmem precedence, load-use
bubble, M launch-once and held response rules. Invalid bundles cannot
forward, redirect, launch arithmetic, access memory or retire. Preserve
full reset, payload/control squash split, decoder default-illegal
validation, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, aligned memory masks, every
existing trap and monotonically consecutive channel-zero RVFI orders.
Maintain nret=1 and all top-level ports and benchmark/evaluator contracts.

Predict eight percent fitness improvement with low confidence, from
shorter ordinary arithmetic/branch feedback at unchanged CoreMark
cycles. This is a prediction, not an accepted measured result. At
4,296,444 cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above 98.133 MHz
and fitness above 228.405 iterations/sec. Register and prefix routing
costs, shifter/result-selection delay, multiplier control and the extra
bitwise preparation after forwarding can erase the gain. Require actual
median vendor timing and marker-bounded cycles; area or a shorter logic
path alone is insufficient. Run unchanged formal, real arithmetic,
RVFI cosimulation and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker gates.

title: Register predictor-event eligibility before execution
motivation:
The champion already removes most predictable direct-control bubbles.
Prior folded indexing saved only 0.29% of CoreMark cycles; agree tables,
registered lookup, local saturation and queued training all reduced
Fmax. Fresh isolated trials of fetch-counter snapshots, smaller tables,
one-bit history indexing and balanced comparison also failed to beat
the champion in their measured placement configurations. The current
recovery and training equations nevertheless use general ex_advance,
which includes !busy from multiply/divide completion. Legal branches
and jumps cannot be M operations, but separately registered control
bits hide that relationship from synthesis. Registering the event class
explicitly can remove unrelated arithmetic-completion control from
predictor recovery and BHT writes without changing guesses or latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add two one-bit predictor eligibility fields to id_ex_t. When ID admits
a valid instruction, register resolve_eligible as
!dec_is_illegal && (dec_is_branch || dec_is_jump), and train_eligible as
!dec_is_illegal && dec_is_branch && (in.direct_target[1:0] == 2'b00).
Compute these predicates from the validated decoder and the fetched
instruction's own direct target, before the existing ID/EX boundary.
Reset both bits to zero, clear both on flush or an advancing invalid
fetch, and otherwise hold them with the instruction during ID stalls.
Follow the existing prediction-control ownership and priority exactly;
do not reinstate flush gating on ordinary ID/EX payload flops.

In EX define prediction_accept = in.valid && !reset && !stall. Set
redirect to prediction_accept && in.resolve_eligible &&
(actual_nonsequential ^ in.predicted_taken), and branch_update to
prediction_accept && in.train_eligible. These two predictor events
must not depend on busy, ex_advance, M request acceptance or M response
validity. Keep general ex_advance and its !busy qualification unchanged
for execution, bypassing and arithmetic transfers. No M operation can
set either predictor eligibility bit: the decoder's legal branch/jump
matches have the ordinary ALU_ADD default and no M operation controls.
This is a change to prediction-event qualification, not permission to
advance a genuinely occupied execution instruction.

Keep branch comparisons, target calculation, actual_nonsequential,
misalignment and illegal traps, redirect_target, resolved RVFI pc_next,
jump links, EX/MEM progression and all arithmetic protocols unchanged.
In particular an aligned legal conditional branch trains once on its
accepted EX cycle whether taken or not, while a misaligned direct
target never trains. Misaligned JAL/JALR and taken branches retain
the existing trap and link-suppression rules. Recovery continues to
defer during an older dmem hold and overrides younger imem/load-use
holds on release. Bubbles and wrong-path instructions clear both
eligibility bits and all existing side-effect controls.

Preserve the existing 128-entry two-bit BHT, PC[8:2] indexing, live
saturating updates, weakly-not-taken reset, instruction-qualified
direct-target prediction, direct JAL prediction, sequential JALR,
exact saved predicted_taken, direction-XOR checking and all pipeline
boundaries. Do not add history, a return stack, a target table, a
training queue or another recovery stage. This single predictor angle
moves static event eligibility to ID and separates prediction-event
acceptance from unrelated M completion.

Expect six percent higher fitness through Fmax at unchanged CoreMark
cycles, with low confidence because ALU-result and load forwarding
remain competing paths. At 4,296,444 marker-bounded cycles acceptance
requires more than approximately 98.133 MHz median Gowin Fmax and
fitness above 228.40456 iter/sec. Require an identical prediction,
training and retirement trace for a fixed program and ready sequence;
any added recovery cycle is a failure of this hypothesis. Validate the
registered eligibility against decoder legality and control class,
including all M operations and reserved encodings, then run the
unchanged formal, stalled RVFI cosimulation and canonical CoreMark
CRC, UART-validation, MMIO-bracket and bounded-memory gates. Keep
nret=1, architectural operand retention and consecutive RVFI order.

title: Canonicalize accepted M controls to remove branch-fault write dependencies
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz. EX currently routes
operand-dependent branch/jump alignment faults into M launch, saved M
write controls and forwarding qualification. Validated RV32M decoding
guarantees that an accepted M instruction writes a register, is legal,
and is neither a memory operation nor control flow. Storing those
guaranteed controls as constants can remove redundant state and late
branch-comparison dependencies from arithmetic acceptance and bypass.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one micro-optimization: canonicalize the control state of accepted
legal MUL/DIV transactions and use the resulting ownership invariant
to factor their launch, completion and forwarding gates. Keep every
pipeline boundary, arithmetic latency, operation tag, operand register,
predictor decision, bypass data source and memory handshake unchanged.

Keep combined misalign_fault and ctrl_with_trap for ordinary EX/MEM
payloads, PC resolution, redirect suppression and RVFI trap reporting.
Taken misaligned branches and misaligned JAL/JALR must still trap;
misaligned jumps must still suppress the link write. No alignment or
decoder-legality check is removed or weakened.

Retain every current M launch condition except that its write/legal
qualification uses in.ctrl.reg_write && !in.ctrl.is_illegal instead
of the branch/jump-adjusted ctrl_with_trap fields. Prove from the
unchanged decoder that an accepted M instruction cannot have either
control-flow alignment fault. Illegal instructions cannot launch.

On that accepted launch, save the original execute_payload and override
only its ctrl field with a canonical M control bundle. Start the bundle
at zero; copy the original alu_op; set reg_write=1, mem_width=2 and
mem_sext=1. All other fields are zero, including is_illegal, mem_read,
mem_write, mem_to_reg, branch_op, alu_src, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr,
is_lui and is_auipc. This must equal the original validated decoder
bundle for every one of the eight M operations. Preserve the original
instruction, PC/next-PC, destination and architectural operand values.
Preserve full reset, launch-once capture, response hold and transfer
clearing of both saved records. Explicit constants should let synthesis
merge saved reg_write with saved valid and eliminate illegal/memory
metadata flops and their branch-fault input cones.

Under the proved invariant saved.valid implies that its owner was an
accepted legal register-writing non-memory M instruction, qualify M
transfer with the unchanged in.valid, class, reset, stall, result_valid
and saved.valid conditions. The saved reg_write/illegal tests are then
redundant and may be omitted from this transfer gate. In the M arms of
bypass_w_en, use the matching qualified transfer instead of rechecking
saved reg_write, is_illegal and mem_read. Retain ex_advance, nonzero
saved destination, captured destination selection and all class routing.
Prove the ownership implication across launch, waits, response holds,
transfer and reset; do not assume it without proof.

In ordinary non-M forwarding, retain raw decoder reg_write, legality,
load exclusion and misalign_jump qualification. Branch-only alignment
need not feed this register-write gate because decoded conditional
branches never write a register. Keep trap-adjusted ordinary retirement
controls intact. Preserve EX-over-MEM-over-RF priority and every data mux.
All these changes implement the same canonical write-control invariant;
do not add comparator, predictor, ALU, operand-mux or retiming changes.

A preliminary write-factoring probe without canonical saved controls
passed all 35 existing real pipeline tests and a symbolic decoder proof.
Its Gowin placements reached 90.797, 86.182 and 86.182 MHz, a regression.
The final canonical-state proposal is unmeasured: its intended benefit
is removing the saved control dependency and redundant completion gates
that the preliminary probe retained. Those preliminary checks do not
establish a fitness gain or replace validation of this final circuit.
Predict eight percent higher fitness with low confidence; ordinary ALU
and accepted-load forwarding remain competing timing limits.

Preserve nret=1 and all core ports, default-illegal validated decoding,
EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, exact real RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic,
architectural operands, traps and side-effect suppression, reset and
squash priorities, memory acceptance, predictor training and consecutive
RVFI order. Run unchanged formal, real arithmetic and stalled ISS cosim
gates. Require canonical CoreMark CRCs, its validation literal, bounded
memory and original MMIO timing brackets. At the expected unchanged
4,296,444 measured cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above
about 98.133 MHz and fitness above 228.405 iter/sec. Measure all three
canonical placement options and actual cycles before claiming a gain.

title: Separate operand-candidate registers from bypass-source selection
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. The recurring timing limit is EX/MEM
result or completion qualification through the ID forwarding network
into younger registered operands. r3s1 successfully registered final
operands, and r4s1 registered multiply responses, but r6s1's unregistered
six-candidate crossbar and r10s1's arithmetic preparation regressed.
More fetch buffering does not address this feedback: scratch five-slot
registered-head queues passed canonical CoreMark at 4,061,023 cycles,
but tested Gowin placement-option-zero Fmax values were only 77.818 to
82.696 MHz. Even actual LUT-RAM extraction and 1,196 registers left
operand/control feedback critical. Do not implement those queue probes.
The next structural opportunity is to register candidate values and
dependency decisions separately, removing acceptance-qualified wide
operand selection from the result-to-register path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace ID's resolved-operand register boundary with a registered
operand-candidate bank and registered source tags. This is one structural
retiming of operand resolution, not a new frontend or arithmetic design.
Preserve the champion's live fetch, predictor, stage count, ordinary
instruction latency, load-use bubble, memory stages and divider.

On each real ID admission, independently capture two write-first RF
values, one shared current EX architectural-result candidate and one
shared completing-MEM architectural-result candidate. Register separate
rs1/rs2 source tags with the owning instruction: RF, EX candidate, MEM
candidate, or architectural zero. Determine tags with the existing
EX-over-MEM-over-RF priority, nonzero destination matches, actual producer
advance/completion and final trap-qualified writes. Preserve conservative
matching of both raw encoded source fields for exact RVFI values.
Capture EX and MEM candidate buses without their write-eligibility muxes;
eligibility determines tags, never the candidate data or its write enable.
Ineligible candidate bits are harmless because no valid consumer selects
them. A load's EX address must never receive an EX-value tag.

Remove the existing resolved rs1_val/rs2_val and final alu_a/alu_b
storage from ID/EX. Replace those four 32-bit words with rf_rs1,
rf_rs2, ex_candidate and mem_candidate, plus the two small source tags.
Retain instruction PC, immediate, destination/source addresses, original
decoded controls, prediction and saved direct target. Thus candidate
storage replaces existing operand words rather than duplicating them.
Fully reset all new registers. Candidate payloads use one raw hold
consisting only of load-use, EX busy and dmem hold, without redirect or
imem-valid terms. Reset/flush/invalid-fetch policy for controls and valid
remains complete; correction separately invalidates ownership and wins
over raw holds. A correction may leave arbitrary inactive candidate
payload, but cannot admit, execute or retire that payload.

EX resolves architectural rs1/rs2 solely from its own registered bank
and tags, then selects PC/immediate ALU sources using registered controls.
Combine source-tag and PC/immediate selection into a shallow masked
selection tree; do not add a serial RF/EX/MEM mux followed by two further
x0 and immediate muxes. Tags and selection controls are all registered.
The candidate data path never traverses forward_unit eligibility before
entering its bank. Store data, branches, JALR, divider requests and saved
RVFI operands use these same resolved architectural values. EX/MEM and
MEM/WB retain their architectural metadata meanings. An ID/EX hold keeps
all candidates and tags together, so draining WB or changing memory data
cannot change an already admitted instruction's operands.

Keep the current accepted EX result bus, including link values and held
M responses, and the exact accepted-load extraction path. The new timing
recurrence is registered candidates/tags -> EX local selection -> ALU
and architectural result mux -> candidate register. Producer qualification
and dependency matching end at narrow tag registers in parallel. This
differs from r6s1: it does not enlarge a combinational ID crossbar or
drive its wide data mux with unregistered completion/trap eligibility.
It also differs from the pre-r3 pipeline: EX never reads a live regfile
or live MEM bypass bus before arithmetic. Only instruction-owned flops
feed execution.

Protect the multiplier from the new local selection prefix. Add one
private operand-capture step to mul_unit: accept resolved operands and
operation into request registers, then compute the existing shared
signed 33-by-33 product into its held response on the next edge. Product
selection and all RV32M signs remain exact. This adds one cycle per
multiply, while keeping the DSP input timing independent of the EX
source-selection mux. ALTOPS uses the same request ownership and capture
step with the exact existing formulas, applied to every operand pair.
Keep division's existing request capture/PREP/iteration/sign/response
protocol and its real/ALTOPS arithmetic unchanged. M requests launch
once, older stages drain, and responses remain stable until accepted.

An immediately dependent load still waits one bubble and then captures
the accepted MEM value into its candidate bank. No extra ordinary ALU,
branch, load or store stage or interlock is allowed. Dmem stalls retain
EX/MEM and ID/EX, prevent premature tags and M transfers, and suppress
duplicate retirement. Invalid, trapped or squashed instructions cannot
forward, redirect, train, launch M operations, access memory or retire.
Preserve decoder default-illegal validation, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality,
all alignment traps and byte masks, complete architectural reset,
nret=1, exact top-level IO and consecutive channel-zero RVFI orders.
Modify no benchmark, evaluator, wrapper, contract file or other core.

Predict twelve percent fitness improvement with low confidence. This
final candidate-bank topology is unmeasured; the failed queue probes
provide negative evidence only. It relocates selection delay rather
than eliminating it, so ALU feedback, narrow tag qualification, local
branch selection or accepted-load capture may still limit Fmax. Each
multiply adds one cycle; the r3/r4 cycle difference suggests roughly
94,172 extra cycles as an approximate workload reference, not a measured
count for this design. At 4,390,616 cycles, acceptance needs median
Fmax above about 100.284 MHz and fitness above 228.405 iter/sec. Require
actual marker-bounded cycles and median Gowin timing; correctness or a
shorter logic cone alone does not establish improvement. Run unchanged
formal, real M arithmetic tests, exact stalled RVFI cosimulation and
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/marker gates.

Adapt bundle layouts and test EX/MEM/RF candidate tag priority,

title: Resolve return bubbles with a small EX-trained return stack
motivation:
The champion already predicts aligned JAL and conditional branches, but
every JALR still redirects and discards a younger fetch. Prior predictor
banking, queued training, lookup retiming and event eligibility changes
regressed vendor Fmax; folded indexing reduced CoreMark cycles only 0.29%.
Predicting ordinary function returns is a distinct remaining source of
avoidable control bubbles and can preserve the working BHT implementation.

hypothesis.motivation:

every JALR still redirects and discards a younger fetch. Prior predictor

Predicting ordinary function returns is a distinct remaining source of

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one eight-entry return-address stack used only to predict canonical
returns: legal JALR with funct3=0, rd=x0, rs1=x1 or x5, and immediate zero.
Predict an aligned, valid stack top; an empty stack uses the champion's
sequential JALR policy. Retain the existing 128-entry two-bit conditional
predictor, its PC[8:2] indexing, saturation/reset/training semantics,
instruction-derived direct targets and always-taken aligned JAL prediction.

Update the stack only once on a valid legal aligned jump advancing from
EX into EX/MEM. Push pc+4 for JAL or JALR writing x1 or x5; pop for the
canonical returns above. Other indirect jumps have no stack action and
continue to resolve normally. Use a circular eight-entry payload array,
three-bit next-write pointer and four-bit bounded occupancy. On a full
push overwrite the oldest entry and retain count eight. On a nonempty pop
decrement pointer and count; never underflow. Reset pointer and occupancy;
payload entries need no reset and must be masked whenever count is zero.
This is EX-trained predictor state, so wrong-path fetches never mutate it
and no speculative stack checkpoint or recovery walk is required. Adjacent
call/return sequences may see an old top and recover; do not add a late
combinational EX-to-fetch stack bypass to chase this uncommon case.

Carry the exact return target selected at accepted fetch and a return-
prediction-valid bit through IF/ID and ID/EX, separately from the existing
direct_target. Capture them with the instruction, hold them during all ID
stalls, and clear prediction validity with every reset, flush or invalid
bubble. Set predicted_taken when IF actually chooses the return target.
In EX preserve direction-XOR correction for direct branches/JAL, and add
target verification only for a saved valid return prediction: correct if
the architectural aligned legal JALR target differs from that saved target,
or if the predicted return traps. A taken prediction with a wrong target
cannot be validated by direction XOR alone. The resolved rs1+imm value
with bit zero cleared remains the source of redirect_target and RVFI
pc_next. Stack contents must never determine architectural jump targets,
links, trap decisions or register operands. Use a balanced equality
reduction for the target check, independent of conditional BHT training.

Preserve existing PC correction priority over imem/load-use stalls and
defer correction and stack updates during older dmem holds or EX occupancy.
Accept a fetch prediction only on the same edge admitting its instruction;
do not push/pop on repeated stalled fetches, bubbles or squashed instructions.
Clear all younger side-effect controls on correction exactly as today.
Keep nret=1 IO, strict RVFI order, all legality/alignment traps, operand
forwarding and retention, memory handshakes and real/ALTOPS M arithmetic.
Change only predictor state, metadata, target verification and its wiring.

Forecast six percent higher fitness with low confidence: removed return
bubbles must outweigh the added top-read and JALR-target-check timing cost.
This is an unmeasured hypothesis, not a claimed benchmark improvement.
Acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax_Hz times ten divided by marker-
bounded CoreMark cycles greater than 228.40456 iterations/second. Validate
empty/full stacks, overflow/underflow, nested calls using x1 and x5,
consecutive calls/returns, altered link-register values, illegal/misaligned
JALR, reset, every bus/interlock hold and wrong-path calls/returns. Require
exact RVFI PC/next-PC/results/traps/order and absence of wrong-path stores,
unchanged formal/cosim gates, all five canonical CoreMark CRCs, validation
literal, bounded accesses and MMIO timing brackets before scoring timing.

title: Register memory lane formatting at the existing EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
Accepted-load forwarding from MEM into ID remains a competing timing
limit: r8s0 and r10s1 reported critical u_mem-to-u_id paths. Currently
MEM decodes access width and effective-address alignment before granting
bypass eligibility, and also formats the timed memory write outputs.
Earlier wider operand crossbars and ID arithmetic preparation regressed.
Precomputing these small memory transaction fields in EX can simplify
MEM's acceptance and output cones without changing pipeline scheduling.
