hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move memory lane-mask generation, store-byte replication and access
alignment checking across the existing EX/MEM register. This is one
local combinational retiming optimization; keep all stage boundaries,
instruction latencies, bypass data sources and memory handshakes.

Extend ex_mem_t with a four-bit lane_mask and a one-bit mem_misalign.
Compute both from the instruction's effective address and decoded width
when constructing execute_payload in EX. Use precisely the existing
rules: byte mask 0001 shifted by address[1:0]; halfword mask 0011 shifted
by address[1:0]; otherwise mask 1111. A memory operation is misaligned
for width two when either low address bit is set, or for width one when
address bit zero is set; byte accesses are always aligned. Non-memory
operations must have mem_misalign zero. Preserve the current behavior
of every width encoding, including deterministic inactive controls.

Repurpose EX/MEM write_data to carry the already formatted store bus
value: four copies of rs2[7:0] for byte, two copies of rs2[15:0] for half,
otherwise the original rs2 word. Continue carrying the original resolved
architectural rs2 independently in rs2_val for RVFI. Do not format or
modify ID/EX operands, ALU inputs, divider inputs or multiplier inputs.
Define the new fields as part of the complete execute payload, including
saved arithmetic payloads, so reset, EX/MEM hold, transfer and whole-bundle
bubble clearing retain exactly their current ownership and priorities.

MEM consumes the registered lane mask, formatted write_data and alignment
flag instead of recomputing them from width and address. Drive dmem_wdata
directly from the formatted field. Preserve the existing request gates:
dmem_wen is the saved mask only for mem_write and no alignment fault;
dmem_ren is mem_read and no alignment fault. Keep dmem_addr as the original
effective byte address. Apply the saved alignment fault to the existing
MEM trap-adjusted control bundle, suppressing reg_write and setting
is_illegal exactly as before. Bypass eligibility must still require valid,
no reset, actual MEM acceptance, permitted register write, no trap and
nonzero rd. It must never bypass a held load or unaccepted read data.

Leave load extraction and its sign/zero extension, bypass_data selection,
aligned RVFI memory address, MEM/WB data retention, WB selection and every
pipeline interlock unchanged. RVFI masks and store data consume the same
saved mask and formatted data used by the bus. While io_dmemReady is zero,
every request field and new metadata bit holds with EX/MEM; completion
and retirement still happen exactly once. Misaligned accesses continue
to trap without issuing memory requests. Invalid bubbles retain cleared
side-effect controls and cannot access memory or advertise a producer.

The intended gain is a shorter MEM-to-ID producer-qualification path and
fewer post-register memory-output muxes. Low address bits require only
bounded local arithmetic in EX, while store formatting uses the already
registered rs2. The additional EX-side fanout and five metadata flops can
instead move the limit into EX, and load extraction remains unchanged.
Predict eight percent higher fitness with low confidence. This final
circuit is unmeasured. Local carry-select, shared-shifter, operand/WB-mux,
link-routing and comparator probes all regressed on placement option zero;
exclude those changes. Their equivalence checks do not validate this
different proposal or establish any fitness gain.

Preserve nret=1 and exact core IO, reset and squash semantics, decoder
default-illegal validation, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, all alignment
traps, exact real and ALTOPS RV32M arithmetic, prediction/training and
consecutive RVFI order. Require unchanged formal, exact stalled ISS
cosimulation and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/OOB/MMIO-bracket gates.
The expected canonical measured cycle count remains 4,296,444. Acceptance
needs actual fitness above 228.40456 iterations/second, approximately
98.133 MHz median Gowin Fmax at that cycle count. Measure all three
canonical placement options rather than inferring gain from logic depth.

title: Register execution results before operand forwarding
motivation:
The champion reaches 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Successful structural changes isolated
division, registered resolved operands, and registered multiplication.
The remaining recurring path crosses EX arithmetic and acceptance
qualification into the next ID operand registers. r6s1 widened the
unregistered crossbar, r10s1 moved carry preparation into accepted-load
capture, and r11s1 moved selection after the operand registers; all
regressed. Their common weakness is preserving a same-cycle execution
result-to-younger-operand recurrence. A genuine additional result
register offers a different timing tradeoff with an explicit IPC cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one in-order registered execution-result stage between current EX
and MEM. Retain ID's fully resolved architectural operands and final
ALU input registers. EX computes a complete result transaction into
this new register; a subsequent result stage forwards only registered
results and transfers the transaction to the existing EX/MEM memory
register. Remove every combinational current-EX-result-to-ID data path.
This is one structural pipeline-depth change, retaining single issue,
the current fetch predictor, register file, ALU arithmetic and memory
interface. Ordinary independent instructions still issue every cycle.

Resolve dependencies before ID admission. A valid writing instruction
still computing in EX is unavailable to ID; hold fetch and inject an
ID/EX bubble on a destination match. A registered non-load result in
the new stage can forward directly to ID, followed in priority by
completing MEM and write-first WB/RF. An immediate ALU-result consumer
gains one interlock cycle. A load is unavailable in both EX and the
new result stage and becomes available only on accepted MEM completion,
so its immediately dependent consumer gains two interlock cycles total.
Match both raw encoded source fields to preserve the existing exact
RVFI operand convention, including fields unused by execution. Never
let an older MEM/RF value override a younger unavailable writer.

Register branch condition, resolved next-PC, final alignment/trap
controls, prediction correction and training metadata with the result
transaction. Apply a correction exactly once from the new stage on
transfer, when older MEM is not stalled. Kill the younger current EX
instruction and ID admission, including an arithmetic-unit request
that would otherwise launch on that edge. Suppress its memory effects,
forwarding and retirement. Predicted-correct branches add no mandatory
issue bubble; corrections have one additional recovery cycle. Keep
direct-target direction-XOR checking and exact JALR alignment behavior.

Dmem backpressure holds the memory request and both upstream occupied
execution registers, with MEM/WB valid cleared to avoid repeats.
Dependency bubbles drain older results rather than holding an already
completed instruction. Imem backpressure invalidates only new fetch
admission and permits older stages to drain. Multiply/divide launch
once from registered operands and retain responses until the new
result register can accept them; a downstream correction cancels any
younger arithmetic ownership. Retain all real and ALTOPS formulas.
Reset every new ownership bit, and clear all side-effect controls in
invalid transactions. Preserve complete architectural reset, decoder
default-illegal validation, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, alignment
traps, byte masks, nret=1 and the exact single-channel IO/RVFI contract.

Predict twelve percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The
critical test is whether isolating EX arithmetic from ID forwarding
raises median Gowin Fmax enough to pay for measured dependency and
correction bubbles. At a hypothetical 20 percent cycle increase,
acceptance requires Fmax above approximately 117.76 MHz; this is a
break-even calculation, not a timing measurement. Run the unchanged
formal/cosimulation gates and canonical CRC/UART/OOB/marker checks,
then compare actual CoreMark cycles times median Gowin Fmax against
the 228.405 iter/sec acceptance floor. Do not infer success from
fewer logic levels or a single placement result.

title: Forward fetched counter state to remove the BHT training read
motivation:
The champion's 128-entry bimodal predictor performs an asynchronous
fetch lookup and a second, independently addressed counter lookup for
EX training. Saturation then feeds a wide indexed write. Recent timing
includes a 38-cell registered-branch-operand to BHT-register path.
Prior one-bit agree prediction lost two-bit hysteresis and regressed;
queued training, banking, registered fetch lookup and eligibility
retiming also regressed. Folded indexing and return prediction saved
less than 0.4 percent of CoreMark cycles. Preserve the successful policy
and target the extra training lookup without delaying its writes.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's 128-entry bimodal predictor performs an asynchronous
fetch lookup and a second, independently addressed counter lookup for
EX training. Saturation then feeds a wide indexed write. Recent timing
includes a 38-cell registered-branch-operand to BHT-register path.
Prior one-bit agree prediction lost two-bit hysteresis and regressed;
queued training, banking, registered fetch lookup and eligibility
retiming also regressed. Folded indexing and return prediction saved
less than 0.4 percent of CoreMark cycles. Preserve the successful policy
and target the extra training lookup without delaying its writes.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the BHT's second read with fetched counter metadata plus one
forwarding record for the most recent applied update. Retain exactly
128 resettable two-bit counters indexed by PC[8:2], weakly-not-taken
reset, asynchronous current-PC prediction, instruction qualification,
aligned instruction-derived targets, always-taken aligned JAL and
sequential JALR. Keep the champion's table organization and all pipeline
boundaries. This is one predictor training-path change.

Expose the complete two-bit counter selected by the existing fetch
lookup in if_id_t, and capture it with the accepted instruction in
id_ex_t. This is the PRE-WRITE counter from that acceptance edge, not
the predicted direction bit. Hold it with the instruction on ID stalls;
reset it with the bundle and allow the existing payload-only update
policy on squash. An invalid instruction cannot train. EX exports that
saved two-bit counter alongside its unchanged branch_update, index and
outcome. Do not reread counters[branch_index] anywhere in training.

In IF retain last_valid, last_index[6:0] and last_counter[1:0] for the
most recent applied branch update. Reset last_valid; retain the record
across non-update cycles, bubbles and every bus/interlock hold. For an
accepted training event choose base_counter = last_counter when
last_valid && last_index == branch_index, otherwise use the instruction's
saved fetch counter. Compute both saturating successor values from this
two-bit base in parallel, then select taken versus not-taken with the
resolved outcome. On the SAME edge as the champion's branch_update,
write the selected two-bit value at branch_index and save that index
and value in the forwarding record. Write and record even a saturated
unchanged value so the record always describes the latest event. There
is no extra training register, queued write, fetch bypass or table
banking. Use compact two-bit Boolean saturation logic, with the outcome
selecting completed values rather than preceding the state calculation.

The forwarding record is required for exact live-counter semantics:
an older branch can train the same index on the edge accepting a younger
branch, whose fetch snapshot still contains the old value. Only one
older instruction occupies EX, and an accepted instruction becomes the
sole EX owner after that edge. While it is held, no other branch can
train. Thus only the most recent applied update can supersede its
snapshot. A matching record supplies that updated value; a nonmatching
record leaves the snapshot current. Consecutive aliases and taken
self-loops must therefore match the champion's counters and predictions
exactly, including under stalls. A naive saved-counter-only update is
explicitly insufficient. If this ownership property does not hold in
the implementation, fail validation rather than tolerate stale updates.

Keep branch_update on the existing valid, legal, aligned EX-to-EX/MEM
acceptance event, with identical reset, dmem hold and arithmetic-busy
qualification. Keep EX direction-XOR correction and its same-cycle
priority over younger imem/load-use holds. Fetch reads observe the
pre-write table state on a simultaneous write, exactly as today.
Preserve every control/valid/prediction squash, payload hold, resolved
architectural next PC, link result, trap check, forwarding rule, memory
handshake, real/ALTOPS M behavior, nret=1 ports and strict RVFI order.
Modify only permitted bench RTL and unit tests.

Removing the independent 128-way training read and its saturation
feedback should reduce LUT muxing and routing while keeping CoreMark
cycles identical. Forecast six percent fitness improvement with low
confidence: unchanged ALU/operand-forwarding paths still compete for
Fmax, and past predictor simplifications have regressed placement.
This is unmeasured, not a claimed improvement. At 4,296,444 measured
cycles acceptance needs median Gowin Fmax above about 98.133 MHz and
fitness above 228.40456 iter/sec, using median Fmax_Hz times ten divided
by marker-bounded cycles. Any predictor-policy change or extra recovery
cycle violates this hypothesis's intended equivalence.

An independent one-EX-owner reference model exercised 600,000 cycles,
212,267 updates, 66,812 matching-record forwardings, 145,495 held EX
cycles, 40 reset cycles and 64,391 saturated updates. The proposed base
counter matched the live training counter on every update, and all 128
table entries matched after every edge. This checks the forwarding
rule only; it is neither implemented-RTL correctness nor FPGA timing
evidence and does not replace the required gates.

Validate against a live-counter reference with same-index consecutive
branches, different-PC aliases, alternating outcomes, both saturation

ALU-to-ID path. Local result-predecode and branch-comparator probes did
not improve median timing; the dedicated branch tree removed the long
branch chain but left ALU-to-memory and ALU-to-ID paths limiting. Target
the addition carry network itself while retaining the successful pipeline.

preparation regressed by moving timing pressure into MEM-to-ID preparation.

entirely in EX, with no carry preparation or extra registers in ID.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only ALU_ADD's 32-bit addition with an explicit sparse carry
prefix over eight four-bit groups. Keep all pipeline boundaries, ordinary
one-cycle execution, live EX forwarding, operation encodings, control and
arithmetic-unit protocols unchanged. This is one local combinational
adder implementation change; its benefit must come entirely from Fmax,
with identical CoreMark iterations per cycle.

For group j=0..7, slice a_j=a[4*j +: 4] and b_j=b[4*j +: 4]. Compute
P_j = &(a_j ^ b_j) and G_j = ({1'b0,a_j}+{1'b0,b_j})[4], using an
explicit five-bit intermediate for the latter. These are group carry
propagate and carry generate with zero incoming carry. Build inclusive
prefix pairs (G,P) in three static parallel levels at distances 1, 2
and 4. A higher group H composed with a lower group L has
  G = G_H | (P_H & G_L);
  P = P_H & P_L.
At each level, nodes whose index is below the distance pass through;
other nodes combine with the corresponding node from the PREVIOUS
level. Never read a partially updated level or create a recursive
full-width priority chain. After the final level, carry into group zero
is zero and carry into group j>0 is prefix_G[j-1].

Compute each four-bit output slice as the low four bits of an explicitly
sized local a_j+b_j+carry_j addition. This leaves only short native
carry chains within groups and a three-level inter-group prefix instead
of a 32-bit serial carry recurrence. Express all group boundaries and
prefix distances with static generate indices or fixed-width vectors,
using portable combinational SV accepted by Gowin, Verilator and Yosys.
Keep the implementation local to alu.sv, avoiding source-list edits.
Do not implement two speculative whole-word carry-select sums, a dense
32-node bit prefix, or an operand-dependent early-exit path. Do not force
LUT boundaries with syn_keep attributes. Confirm synthesis retains the
intended bounded group structure rather than reconstructing a long
word-wide adder or introducing latches.

Route only ALU_ADD through this result. Preserve SUB, signed/unsigned
SLT, all bitwise and shift expressions, LUI, the ALU port contract and
default-zero behavior exactly. Preserve every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS
operation-specific formula unchanged and keep the real registered
M datapaths and their inactive ALU outputs unchanged. Do not alter the
separate PC increment, JALR target adder, branch comparator, predictor,
MEM extraction, result/operand muxes or forwarding qualification.

The new result must equal (a+b) modulo 2^32 for EVERY operand pair,
including overflow; no dependence on opcode history, memory layout or
benchmark data is permitted. Loads, stores, ADD/ADDI and AUIPC retain
their existing effective-address/result semantics. Preserve nret=1
and exact core IO, decoder default-illegal validation, EBREAK-only
SYSTEM legality, all alignment traps and side-effect suppression,
M launch-once/held-response ownership, reset/flush/hold priorities,
memory handshakes, branch recovery/training and strict RVFI order.

Predict eight percent higher fitness with low confidence. This final
adder is unmeasured. Its extra P/G logic and local sum routing can erase
the carry-depth gain, and unchanged branch, shifter or accepted-load
paths can remain limiting. Failed local predecode/comparator prototypes
are negative evidence, not a claimed improvement for this different
circuit. Expected canonical CoreMark cycles remain exactly 4,296,444;
acceptance requires actual fitness above 228.40456 iter/sec, about
98.133 MHz median Gowin Fmax at that cycle count. Measure all three
scored vendor placement options and actual marker-bounded cycles.

Prove combinational equivalence to the original addition for symbolic
32-bit a and b. Keep all existing unit assertions and add carry chains
crossing each four-bit boundary, generate/propagate/kill combinations,
all-ones wraparound, alternating-bit patterns, sign extremes and random
pairs. Exercise dependent ADD/ADDI/AUIPC and memory-address consumers
with operands from EX, accepted MEM loads and write-first WB/RF under

title: Retime branch comparison leaves across the operand register boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444 timed CoreMark cycles. Prior structural successes registered resolved operands and isolated multiplication/division. r12s1 registered every execution result, increased cycles 19.71 percent and regressed fitness; r11s1 moved operand selection into EX and regressed sharply. r10s1's preparation of all add/sub/compare operations made accepted-load-to-preparation timing critical. These outcomes argue for a narrow register-boundary change that preserves ordinary arithmetic and instruction latency.

Conditional branches still compare registered 32-bit operands with native relational operators. Several recent reports expose 38-cell paths from rs2 through EX branch comparison into recovery, predictor updates and ID control. The earlier r4s0 balanced comparator gained 14.05 percent over its then-champion without changing cycles, but left the comparison entirely after the operand registers. This proposal instead moves only the two-bit comparison leaves before that existing boundary; it does not retime general arithmetic or add a stage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Partition conditional-branch comparison across the existing ID/EX operand boundary. ID continues to resolve both architectural operands with current advancing-EX, completing-MEM and write-first-RF priority. For each of sixteen two-bit slices, compute unsigned equality and less-than from those exact resolved values and register the two one-bit flags alongside the original rs1_val/rs2_val. Each leaf depends on just four operand bits and fits a LUT4 truth table. Keep all original operand and ALU-input registers; never reconstruct architectural operands from comparison flags.

EX combines the registered leaves in a balanced four-level tree. A node spanning a more-significant group H and less-significant group L produces equal = equal_H AND equal_L and less = less_H OR (equal_H AND less_L). Compose contiguous bit groups in their original significance order. The root gives full unsigned less-than and equality. Signed less-than uses registered operand signs: if signs differ, use rs1's sign; otherwise use unsigned less-than. BEQ/BNE use equality/inverse, BLT/BGE use signed less-than/inverse, and BLTU/BGEU use unsigned less-than/inverse. No 32-bit branch subtractor or relational operator should remain in the core's branch-resolution cone. Leave ALU SLT/SLTU and ADD/SUB/address/JALR arithmetic unchanged.

This is one structural retiming of conditional-branch execution across an existing register boundary. There is no new pipeline stage, instruction buffer, cache, predictor policy, register-file change or additional execution bubble. Fetch prediction, direct targets, EX correction latency and once-per-accepted-EX BHT training stay as in the champion. The balanced combine alone is not the hypothesis: the important boundary is the newly registered, bit-local comparison information.

Capture comparison leaves with exactly the same payload reset, advance and hold enable as their owning resolved operands. Full reset clears the new fields. On load-use, arithmetic occupancy or dmem holds, retain the instruction's leaves together with its operand values. Flush/invalid admission keeps the existing full ctrl/valid/prediction squash; stale leaves in an invalid payload cannot cause a branch, redirect, predictor update or side effect. A dependent branch after a load must capture the accepted sign/zero-extended MEM load value, not its address or an unaccepted bus word. Back-to-back branches and same-destination writers must use their own freshest operand pair; x0 leaves reflect hardwired zero.

Preserve actual_nonsequential and direction-XOR recovery, saved direct targets, all six branch encodings, taken-target alignment traps, untaken misaligned-target behavior, JAL/JALR link and alignment semantics and complete RVFI operand/PC/trap reporting. Keep nret=1 and the exact top-level ports, decoder default-illegal validated matching and EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality. Keep all real RV32M and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arithmetic, launch-once/held-response ownership, memory alignment/masks/handshakes, architectural reset, side-effect-free bubbles and strictly consecutive channel-zero retirement orders.

Predict eight percent higher fitness with low confidence, at unchanged canonical CoreMark cycles. owned two-bit counter cells. Preserve the exact binary state encoding,
PC[8:2] index, reset value 2'b01, counter-MSB direction, instruction and
target-alignment qualification, always-taken aligned JAL and sequential

Generate one local always_ff owner per cell. On reset its state becomes
01; otherwise only its addressed accepted branch update enables a write.
For local old state {h,l}, compute saturated taken successor

completed two-bit values with branch_taken, then capture under the local
write enable. Each successor bit depends only on this cell's two old
bits and the outcome. No training expression may index the counter array

decrement or an outcome-dependent saturation test in the shared enable.

title: Hide fetch stalls with a fall-through instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iter/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444
marker-bounded CoreMark cycles. Registering every execution result
increased cycles 19.71 percent, while retiming comparison and carry
preparation moved timing cost onto the EX/MEM-to-ID operand paths.
The most useful unfinished structural result is r9s1: its strict
two-entry instruction queue reduced CoreMark cycles to 4,110,006,
but 92.585 MHz produced only a 3.16 percent fitness improvement.
That queue imposed an empty-to-refill cycle after every correction.
Retaining its stall overlap while removing that compulsory cycle
offers a route past the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold without
altering execution latency or adding dependency bubbles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the live fetch-to-ID connection with a four-entry circular
instruction queue that falls through when empty. This is one change
to frontend elasticity: decouple fetch acceptance from ID admission,
while allowing a ready fetch at an empty queue to enter the existing
ID/EX register on the same edge. Keep the current instruction-qualified
bimodal predictor, direct-JAL prediction, ordinary execution stages,
registered resolved operands and blocking M units. Preserve EX branch
correction timing and the current single load-use bubble.

Each stationary queue slot stores instruction, exact PC, predicted_taken
and direct_target. Use head/tail pointers and occupancy; never shift or
copy wide payloads on a dequeue. When nonempty, ID sees only the oldest
stored transaction. When empty, ID sees the current raw fetch transaction
and its imemReady-qualified validity. A ready empty-queue fetch accepted
by ID advances the fetch PC but is not also enqueued. If ID is blocked,
the same ready transaction is enqueued and fetch PC still advances once.
When nonempty, pop only on actual ID admission and enqueue a newly ready
fetch whenever capacity exists, including simultaneous pop/refill at
full occupancy. Drive prediction and next-fetch-PC selection from the
fetch PC/instruction at fetch acceptance, never from a dequeued entry.
All buffered metadata belongs to the instruction that originally fetched
it; queued instructions have no prematurely captured register values.

Allow fetch to continue during load-use, EX arithmetic occupancy and
dmem holds until the queue fills. An imem stall prevents only acceptance
of a new bus word: it cannot invalidate or stall an already buffered
head instruction. A full blocked queue holds PC, pointers and entries.
Keep the existing producer-completion qualifications and
EX-over-completing-MEM-over-write-first-RF operand forwarding. The head
instruction remains available during its load-use interlock and captures
the accepted, extracted load value when that interlock ends. During a
blocking multiply/divide, hold ID/EX's resolved operands and ownership
while older memory/writeback work drains and fetch fills available slots.

An accepted EX correction overrides every queue event: invalidate all
entries, reset occupancy/pointers, squash the current ID admission and
set fetch PC to redirect_target. Reject the old-address word on that
edge regardless of imemReady. On the following ready cycle, the empty
queue falls through and admits the target exactly as the champion does;
no queue refill bubble is required. Correctly predicted branches/JAL
retain their queued successors. Older dmem backpressure still defers
EX acceptance and correction. Payload clock enables should use capacity,
ready and raw issue-hold conditions, with correction affecting ownership
and PC; an inactive slot may capture harmless old-path data on a squash
edge if all validity and pointers are cleared. Fully reset new payloads
and ownership bits. Ensure no wrong-path store or M request launches.

Separate the raw dependency/EX-busy/dmem hold used for admission from
the fetch-bus ready signal. Derive ID valid from buffered occupancy or
empty-queue ready fall-through, and derive architectural pop/bypass
admission from that valid, raw hold and absence of correction. Squash
continues to clear every side-effect control, valid and prediction bit
in ID/EX. Keep raw source fields independent of correction; do not mux
a NOP onto the instruction or register-file address bus. Preserve exact
source values even for unused encoded source fields, x0, overlapping
destinations, and held operands after WB drains.

Preserve nret=1, exact top-level IO, consecutive channel-zero RVFI
orders, decoder default-illegal validation, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality,
alignment traps, memory masks and handshake semantics, complete reset,
and every real/ALTOPS M-extension formula and held-response protocol.
Change no evaluator, benchmark, wrapper, contract file or other core.

Predict eight percent greater fitness with low confidence. The measured
strict queue already removed 4.34 percent of cycles; empty fall-through
should recover its correction-refill cost, and four slots can absorb
longer independent bus-stall bursts. These improvements are predictions,
not measurements of this candidate. The main risk is the buffered/head
versus raw-fetch mux extending decode and operand capture timing; queue
control, predictor staleness and extra routing may consume the gain.
Require canonical CRC/UART/OOB/MMIO-marker validation, unchanged formal
and stalled RVFI cosimulation, and measured median Gowin timing. At the
old queue's 4,110,006 cycles, acceptance requires about 93.87 MHz; a
further two percent cycle reduction lowers that requirement to about
91.99 MHz. Score actual cycles and timing against 228.405 iter/sec.

implementation_notes:
# Fall-through instruction queue

Implemented four stationary instruction slots with circular head/tail pointers and occupancy in cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv. Empty ready fetches enter the existing ID/EX register immediately without also entering the queue; blocked empty fetches enqueue once and advance PC. Buffered heads drain independently of imemReady, and a full queue accepts simultaneous pop/refill. Fetch PC and prediction use the accepted raw bus instruction. Accepted EX correction clears all ownership, squashes ID, rejects the old bus transaction and selects the redirect target; the next ready target falls through without a refill cycle. Queue payload enables use ready, capacity and raw issue hold, allowing harmless inactive payload capture on correction.

Separated raw ID dependency/EX-busy/dmem holds from instruction-bus readiness in hazard_unit.sv and wired them in core.sv. if_id_t fields are preserved and documented as instruction-owned transactions. Execution, ID operand capture, forwarding, memory/writeback, decoder, M units, top-level ports and nret=1 were preserved.

Two implementation deviations: slots are explicit 98-bit packed words because the formal Yosys frontend misinterprets unpacked arrays of packed struct typedefs; a redundant five-bit registered read selector selects the four heads or empty fall-through to reduce mux delay before the register file. It adds no instruction ownership or stage latency and follows the binary pointers/count. All payloads and ownership reset completely.

Added a FIFO scoreboard to every pipeline test and six queue tests covering ready empty bypass, blocked empty enqueue, full held stability, full pop/refill, pointer wrap, unready buffered drain, independent long bus stalls, correction at occupancies 0 through 4 with both ready/unready old bus data, target admission on the first ready edge, buffered branch/JAL predictions, overlapping destinations, unused raw source fields, x0, accepted loads, held M operands, wrong-path store/M suppression, and reset at every occupancy. All existing architectural, RVFI, order, memory and latency assertions remain.

Local validation: lint passes without warnings. The complete core unit suite passes (13 pytest runners, including all 41 pipeline cocotb tests and real/ALTOPS M-unit tests). Final RTL make cosim TARGET=bench (NRET=1) passes selftest with and without random instruction/data stalls and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART validation. An independent final CoreMark run reports ebreak=true, oob=false, bench_bracketed=true, start=14,163, stop=4,007,850 and 3,993,687 marker-bounded cycles. All five canonical CRC values and the validation literal match.

Measured Gowin placement options 0/1/2: 73.213 / 88.583 / 88.583 MHz; median 88.583 MHz. Option-0 area: 4,095 logic cells, 1,486 registers, 40 LUT-RAM, 4 BSRAM and 2 DSP. Fitness from the measured median and cycles is 221.807568 iter/sec (+1.579% versus 218.36), below the requested 228.405 iter/sec threshold. Cycle reduction versus the 4,296,444-cycle champion is about 7.05%; timing cost consumes most of that gain. This candidate would need about 91.218 MHz at its measured cycle count to meet the threshold. Main remaining concern is queue mux/routing and recovery/forwarding timing, including placement-option variation.

Formal status: PASS, all 53 checks passed and zero failed on the final full gate, after two correction attempts. Command: RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh; nret=1 automatically selects the unchanged single-channel wrapper/config. The initial run had 52 passes and pc_fwd_ch0 failed: its trace showed a nonempty queue returning zero PC/instruction because Yosys treated the struct array as one packed word. First fix changed to a vector array sized by $bits(if_id_t), but that frontend rejects $bits(type) with a syntax error. Second fix uses the preserved bundle's explicit 98-bit width; a direct Yosys frontend/proc/check run now recognizes the slots as memory and reports zero problems. The final full run passed, including pc_fwd_ch0 and reg_ch0. No wrapper, config or check has been edited.
lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-002-r14s1 (regression, +1.58%): A four-entry circular fetch queue with empty fall-through overlaps fetch with ID holds and avoids correction-refill bubbles, but frontend elasticity must preserve decode/operand timing: 7.05% fewer CoreMark cycles were mostly offset by median Fmax falling from 93.817 to 88.583 MHz.

title: Static backward-taken prediction removes dynamic predictor timing and fanout
motivation:
The champion's 128-entry two-bit BHT removes branch bubbles but adds an
asynchronous prediction mux, an independently addressed training read,
saturating writeback, and broad EX-outcome/update fanout. Recent banked,
registered, snapshot-forwarded and counter-local versions all lowered
median Gowin Fmax, even when CoreMark cycles were unchanged. The earlier
return stack removed only 0.33 percent of cycles. A substantially smaller
predictor is therefore more promising than another training rearrangement:
eliminate dynamic direction state entirely and retain cheap loop-biased
prediction. This is a timing/area tradeoff, not an accuracy improvement.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the dynamic bimodal BHT with one instruction-qualified static
backward-taken/forward-not-taken predictor. For a legal BRANCH opcode and
validated funct3, predict taken iff the B-immediate sign bit instr[31] is
one and the instruction-derived target is word aligned. Continue predicting
every aligned JAL taken, and continue fetching JALR sequentially. Compute
pc+4 and the existing B/J direct target in parallel and select completed
addresses using the static decision. Keep the current combinational IF/ID
interface and all pipeline boundaries.

Delete all 128 two-bit counter registers, counter reset loops, dynamic
fetch lookup, saturation arithmetic and branch-training ports/wires from
IF, EX and core. Do not replace them with a history register, target table,
agree bit, return stack, validity array, or delayed training pipeline. The
benefit sought is removal of predictor state, table muxes and EX-to-BHT
routing pressure from the timed circuit. The static decision uses raw
instruction bits and never depends on redirect, flush, stall or operands.

Carry predicted_taken and direct_target exactly as today with the accepted
instruction. Preserve EX direction-XOR correction, architectural resolved
next PC, PC+4 link writes, JALR bit-zero clearing, and all illegal/misaligned
control-flow traps. A valid aligned direct prediction must use the same
target as EX, so no general predicted-target equality comparator is needed.
Correction still occurs only on a valid EX advance, is deferred by older
dmem holds, and overrides younger imem/load-use holds on release. Preserve
ID/EX's payload-only clock enable and full ctrl/valid/prediction squash.
Fetch PC holds on bus, load-use and arithmetic stalls as before; unavailable
instructions and wrong-path instructions cannot cause architectural writes.
Keep nret=1, every top-level IO, retirement order, memory behavior, forwarding,
and the real and ALTOPS arithmetic unchanged. Modify only the named bench RTL
and permitted unit tests; do not relax any evaluation check.

Expect six percent higher fitness with low confidence. Extra static
mispredictions cost one recovery bubble each and can offset timing savings;
success requires a median Fmax gain larger than the resulting cycle increase
plus the tournament's 4.6 percent acceptance margin. Measure marker-bounded
stalled CoreMark cycles and the actual Gowin median, rather than claiming
that fewer registers automatically improve timing. The current champion is
93.817 MHz at 4,296,444 cycles and fitness 218.36.

JAL, unpredicted JALR, illegal branch funct3 values, misaligned control
targets and reset. Force an EX correction during imem backpressure and
after a branch has been held by older dmem backpressure. Check the exact

title: Remove EX completion gates from consumer-held forwarding selection
motivation:
The champion's timed recurrence reaches from registered EX operands or
alu_op through EX producer qualification, forwarding and ID operand
capture. Destination matching and M predecode attempts retained actual
completion gates and regressed; registering all results increased
CoreMark cycles by 19.71 percent. A different zero-cycle opportunity is
to exploit the existing consumer hold: ID/EX cannot admit a younger
instruction during EX busy or an older dmem stall. Forwarding selection
therefore need not encode those same conditions again. This can remove
busy/result-valid/saved-control feedback from the operand-select cone
without changing pipeline scheduling or arithmetic ownership.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion's timed recurrence reaches from registered EX operands or
alu_op through EX producer qualification, forwarding and ID operand
capture. Destination matching and M predecode attempts retained actual
completion gates and regressed; registering all results increased
CoreMark cycles by 19.71 percent. A different zero-cycle opportunity is

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one micro-optimization: separate the EX candidate used solely for
ID operand selection from the completion-qualified EX producer. Keep
the existing shared bypass_data bus and every ID data mux. Keep the
original bypass_rd and bypass_w_en outputs, including their exact
actual-advance, saved-M-metadata and trap predicates, for stage checks
and verification. They must no longer feed core's ID forwarding
selection; synthesis can prune their unused timed logic.

Add a separate five-bit id_candidate_rd = in.rd and scalar
id_candidate_eligible = in.valid && in.ctrl.reg_write
                        && !in.ctrl.is_illegal
                        && !in.ctrl.mem_read && !misalign_jump.
These are combinational outputs of EX, with no new state. Wire only
these two signals to forward_unit's existing EX destination and enable
inputs. Keep its nonzero-source/destination matching and EX-over-MEM-
over-write-first-RF priority unchanged. Keep completing MEM forwarding
exactly as today. The candidate enable must not depend on ex_advance,
reset, dmem stall, busy, M class, result_valid, transfer, saved.valid
or selected saved destination. ID reset and hold already prevent
consumption when those conditions make a candidate unavailable.

Preserve misalign_jump qualification so misaligned JAL/JALR cannot
supply a link value. Prove from the unchanged decoder that conditional
branches never write a register and that all decoded M operations are
legal non-memory writers without control-flow alignment faults. Keep
the complete existing ctrl_with_trap/misalign_fault logic for actual
advancement, redirects, EX/MEM controls and RVFI; no architectural trap
or completion check is removed. Loads remain excluded from EX candidates.

The crucial correctness condition is equality on consumer admission,

title: Separate the fast ALU bypass from registered M-extension completion
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 iterations/sec at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The structural r12s1 result stage removed live EX forwarding but increased cycles 19.71 percent. R5s1 and r7s1 pipelined multiplication into MEM yet left ordinary bypass and recovery critical. R14s0 predecoded execution classes but retained the shared completion network. The remaining opportunity is to separate ordinary result production from blocking M completion, rather than register every result or repeat a wider frontend queue.

During this proposal turn, an isolated one-slot fall-through fetch probe passed stalled RVFI comparison and canonical CoreMark at 4,057,628 cycles, but Gowin median Fmax was only 78.332 MHz (193.05 iterations/sec). Reject that frontend probe. A first selective M-completion probe passed selftest and all three random-program RVFI comparisons, plus canonical CoreMark at 4,331,635 cycles: only 0.819 percent more than the champion. Its median Fmax was 86.519 MHz, so it also failed acceptance. Its timing path still traversed branch comparison and shared EX/M-unit control into ID/EX clock enables. The proposed topology must therefore separate M launch/completion qualification from branch-trap logic as well as remove M results from the fast bypass. These failed probes provide negative evidence, not a claimed improvement.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Partition execute result ownership into an ordinary fast ALU/link bypass and a registered M-extension completion lane. Preserve the current pipeline depth, frontend predictor, ID's registered resolved operands and final ALU inputs, memory interface, and blocking multiplier/divider arithmetic. The architectural change is that an accepted M response only enters EX/MEM and becomes visible to younger operands through completing MEM; it never competes on the live EX-to-ID bypass bus. Ordinary ALU/link dependencies still issue without new bubbles. Only an immediately dependent M-result consumer gains one interlock cycle.

Register three validated scheduling bits with ctrl_t in ID/EX: is_multiply, is_divide, and early_write. Derive the M classes only from a decoder-validated RV32M OP encoding; multiplication uses funct3[2]=0 and division/remainder funct3[2]=1. early_write means a legal decoded register writer that is neither a load nor an M operation. Clear all three with the entire control bundle on squash or invalid admission, hold them with the original operands, and reset fully. Do not replace default-illegal decoding or accept reserved instruction encodings. These bits describe ownership, not speculative producer availability.

Expose only the ordinary ALU result or PC+4 link value on EX bypass_data and the current instruction's rd on bypass_rd. Remove the multiply/divide response mux, saved-M-destination mux, and M-transfer checks from that bus. Qualify an early producer from its registered early_write, valid, nonzero rd, reset and older dmem acceptance. Apply the jump-specific low-bit alignment check to link writes. Do not put the general conditional-branch comparator, ctrl_with_trap, M ready/valid, or global arithmetic busy into early-producer qualification: decoded early_write is mutually exclusive with loads, conditional branches and M occupancy. Preserve all architectural trap metadata independently, including branch/jump alignment faults and link-write suppression on a misaligned jump.

Make the M lane's request and response control independent of the general branch-comparison/trap cone. A request requires the valid registered legal M-class bit, no reset or older dmem hold, and that unit's request-ready. Those class bits already imply a validated M writer; do not gate launch with branch-adjusted ctrl_with_trap. A response requires the matching current M owner, saved launch ownership, result-valid and downstream acceptance. Keep operation-specific req_op for arithmetic, but use registered class bits for occupancy and completion routing instead of repeatedly decoding alu_op. Use the registered decoded legal ownership controls for any additional qualification; no branch_cond, branch_taken, misalign_branch or branch-adjusted control may feed M request, transfer, busy or response-ready. Preserve branch/JAL/JALR resolve, prediction correction and training timing for their own instructions. This separation is required: the first selective-bypass probe still failed because it left shared qualification intact.

Keep each unit's current accepted-launch snapshot, exact architectural operand/PC/instruction metadata, bounded arithmetic, and stable held-response protocol. While M is busy, hold ID/EX and fetch, drain older MEM/WB work, and insert side-effect-free EX/MEM bubbles. On result acceptance, place the saved instruction and result into EX/MEM exactly once. A stalled older memory request prevents both launch and response transfer. The M instruction retires at its existing boundary; delaying its consumer does not add an M retirement stage. Preserve both real arithmetic and every exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS stand-in, including zero divisors, signed overflow and high-half products. Modify neither arithmetic datapath nor unit latency in this hypothesis.

Extend the current unavailable-producer interlock from EX loads to EX multiply/divide owners. Conservatively match both raw younger source fields, excluding x0, for exact RVFI operand values even when an encoded source is unused by execution. While M is busy, occupancy holds take precedence over dependency bubbling. On the M completion edge, a matching consumer holds fetch and receives an ID/EX bubble while the M result advances into EX/MEM. On the following accepted MEM cycle, that consumer captures the registered M result through the existing MEM bypass. An independent successor may enter ID/EX on the completion edge. Keep the existing one-bubble load-use rule, EX-over-MEM-over-write-first-RF priority, accepted load extraction, held operands after WB drains, and correct overlapping destination behavior. Never forward a younger unavailable producer's stale RF value or a load's effective address.

Predict eight percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The first selective-completion probe establishes only the small cycle cost, not a timing gain. At its 4,331,635-cycle count, acceptance requires median Fmax above 98.937 MHz and fitness above 228.405 iterations/sec. Approximately 102.15 MHz at that count would yield eight percent greater fitness. Removing M response/destination selection and operand-dependent branch qualification from the fast bypass/completion network is intended to supply that gain; ordinary ALU arithmetic, branch correction, accepted-load capture or physical routing can still dominate. Measure the final median over all Gowin placement options and actual bracketed cycles. A shorter RTL path, fewer LUTs or one favorable placement does not establish success.

Preserve nret=1 and exact top-level memory/RVFI IO, one channel-zero retirement per instruction with consecutive orders, decoder legality and EBREAK-only SYSTEM handling, alignment traps and byte masks, complete reset, memory handshakes, no wrong-path side effects, and all hard invariants. Change no evaluator, benchmark, wrapper, contract file or other core. Require the unchanged formal and stalled RVFI cosimulation gates, existing real/ALTOPS arithmetic tests, and canonical CoreMark CRC/UART literal/OOB/MMIO-marker validation. The final topology still needs full formal and directed-unit validation after implementation.

title: Register misprediction recovery without delaying ordinary execution
motivation:
The champion scores 218.36 at 93.817 MHz and 4,296,444 marker-bounded
CoreMark cycles. Repeated BHT storage/training rewrites lowered Fmax;
folded indexing and return prediction saved less than 0.4% of cycles.
Several timing reports expose long EX-to-IF-to-ID recovery paths.
Registering all EX results previously increased cycles 19.71%, because
it also delayed dependency forwarding and every branch correction.
Instead isolate predictor recovery itself: tolerate a second recovery
cycle only when the existing predictor is actually wrong, while keeping
ordinary execution, forwarding and correctly predicted flow unchanged.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register the existing prediction-mismatch decision at the EX/MEM boundary
and reuse that instruction's already registered pc_next as its recovery
target. Retain the champion's 128-entry two-bit
bimodal predictor, PC[8:2] indexing, weakly-not-taken reset, live-counter
training, aligned instruction-derived direct targets, always-taken JAL
and unpredicted JALR. Do not change branch comparisons, multiplier or
divider latency, ordinary result forwarding, fetch/decode boundaries,
or prediction policy. This is one predictor-recovery timing experiment.

EX still computes actual_nonsequential, architectural pc_next, traps,
links and the direction-XOR mismatch from the accepted instruction.
On a valid execution advance, capture one recovery-pending bit with
EX/MEM, using the existing legality/alignment-adjusted mismatch. The
target is the existing resolved
next PC, including sequential recovery for a predicted-taken loop exit
or a trapping prediction. Do not drive IF redirect or ID squash from
the live EX mismatch. In the following cycle the registered recovery
drives the PC correction and the younger-pipeline squash. Recovery
metadata holds with EX/MEM on an older dmem stall and clears on bubbles,
reset and after consumption, so each instruction corrects exactly once.
Keep the resolving instruction's retirement and RVFI pc_next intact.

The added speculative instruction may reach ID/EX before the registered
correction becomes visible. On that correction cycle, explicitly kill
the younger EX owner before it can transfer into EX/MEM, forward a
result, train the BHT, launch an M request or accept an M response.
Clear the complete EX/MEM successor bundle, including memory/write
controls, while the older resolving instruction drains normally to
MEM/WB. Define the externally used redirect solely from the registered
EX/MEM valid/recovery-pending bits and reset; redirect_target comes from
that registered pc_next. Neither may depend on the younger EX owner,
its busy state, its operands or the live mismatch. Suppress wrong-path
busy as well as launch/transfer so a younger
MUL/DIV cannot hold up recovery. Kill dominates younger execution and
occupancy; it must not suppress MEM bypass, WB writeback or retirement
of the older correcting instruction. The wrong-path instruction cannot
have launched an arithmetic request before this cycle in the existing
single-owner pipeline; assert that assumption in directed tests.

On the same correction cycle, flush all ID/EX control, valid and saved
prediction bits and invalidate the combinational IF payload. Give the
registered correction priority over imem-not-ready, load-use and younger
arithmetic holds. Preserve the current payload-only clock-enable policy
and raw instruction/RF-address independence from recovery. A correcting
control instruction is not a dmem access, so the MEM correction does
not depend on io_dmemReady; any preceding older memory stall already
delayed its EX/MEM acceptance. Retain existing dmem interlocks for all
ordinary execution and defer capture while EX cannot advance.

Train conditional counters on the original accepted EX branch event,
exactly once, with an added younger-EX-kill guard. Do not delay training
or add a recovery-to-fetch outcome bypass. Capture the prediction that
IF actually used with each instruction. Correctly predicted branches
and JAL retain zero added bubbles. Every actual correction costs one
extra bubble relative to the champion, rather than penalizing all
dependent ALU operations or adding a permanent frontend stage.

The intended timing change removes the branch comparator, alignment,
mismatch and EX-advance cone from the same-cycle IF PC select and ID
squash/operand-enable path. The new younger-EX kill starts at a single
registered recovery bit. Reusing pc_next avoids duplicate RTL target
storage, but its formerly RVFI-only register now feeds a timed output:
budget up to 32 newly retained target flops plus the recovery bit and
their routing. Other ALU/operand-forwarding paths may still
limit Fmax, so forecast 7% higher fitness with low confidence, not a
claimed result. At a 2% cycle increase, crossing the 4.6% acceptance
margin requires approximately 100.10 MHz median Gowin Fmax; measure
the actual Fmax_Hz times ten divided by marker-bounded cycles and
require fitness greater than 228.40456 iterations/second.
